title: Evangelion reveals new story you can only hear on a Japanese bullet train
summary: Neon Genesis Evangelion is getting a new story, but you can only experience it while riding aboard a bullet train in Japan.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Evangelion reveals new story you can only hear on a Japanese bullet train by James Busby Published: Oct 05, 2026, 15:43 Save for later Save for later Khara Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Neon Genesis Evangelion is getting a new story, but you can only experience it while riding aboard a bullet train in Japan. Following on from the Neon Genesis Evangelion 30th anniversary Asuka short, and the exciting announcement that Yoko Taro is working on a new Eva anime , the popular sci-fi show is getting another new story. However, unlike the 15-minute celebration episode that aired worldwide after it leaked online , only Eva fans who ride Japan’s Tokaido Shinkansen will get to experience a new audio drama featuring Misato Katsuragi and Ritsuko Akagi. Article continues after ad Evangelion gets exclusive bullet train drama According to the translated announcement, “Kansai Travel Plan” follows Misato Katsuragi and Ritsuko Akagi as they prepare a school trip for Shinji and his fellow Eva pilots. To do this, the pair head out on a scouting trip, with Misato planning an outing intended to strengthen the pilots’ bond. It sounds all rather wholesome and just the kind of thing that would be perfect to listen to during a busy commute to school or work. After all, having Shinji screaming while killing Angels isn’t exactly the most relaxing way to start the day. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad Crunchyroll Japanese voice actors Kotono Mitsuishi and Yuriko Yamaguchi will both be reprising their roles as Misato and Ritsuko in the exclusive train drama, too. Listeners will also be eligible for an original acrylic keychain, featuring Shinji, Rei, Asuka, Kaworu, and Mari seated together inside a train carriage. There’s also a keychain styled after a Shinkansen information display up for grabs, for those who are both train and Eva fans. The collaboration between train operator JR Central and Evangelion runs from October 18, 2026, to January 31, 2027, and celebrates the Osaka edition of the series’ 30th anniversary exhibition, “All of Evangelion.” Related Japan’s bullet trains will have anime girls that talk to you during your journey Lycoris Recoil launches bullet train radio show with exclusive merch Neon Genesis Evangelion gets brand-new film for 30th anniversary Article continues after ad For more information on how you can listen along, be sure to check out the campaign website for instructions and merch collection details. title: New anime goes viral for opening with a massive financial warning
summary: A new anime has released a lengthy warning about foreign exchange trading, urging fans to take extra care to avoid any financial risks that could “interfere with one’s daily life”.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime New anime goes viral for opening with a massive financial warning by James Busby Published: Oct 02, 2026, 12:31 Save for later Save for later Crunchyroll Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News A new anime has released a lengthy warning about foreign exchange trading, urging fans to take extra care to avoid any financial risks that could “interfere with one’s daily life”. Warnings that flash up before you settle into a show or game aren’t exactly new, especially for media that involves unsettling themes or imagery. Back in 2025, Silent Hill f famously shocked fans with a warning so intense that it had fans questioning what kind of experience they were in for. Article continues after ad However, a new show about foreign exchange trading (FX Fighter Kurumi-chan) is going viral after its creators have urged viewers to take extra precautions if they decide to get into the high-risk world of buying and selling currencies. FX Fighter Kurumi-chan gives warning over loss of money For those who don’t know, FX Fighter Kurumi-chan follows college student Kurumi Fukuga as she enters the risky world of foreign exchange trading following the tragic death of her mother. Kurumi finds herself taking financial risks, all with the aim of earning back the 20 million yen her mother lost. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad It’s pretty riveting stuff, but as you can imagine, the anime isn’t exactly the kind of thing you put on to wind down with. However, due to the nature of the series, the creators prepared the following warning: “This is a work of fiction. Forex (foreign exchange margin trading) is a high-risk venture, and it’s possible for losses to exceed margin payments. There is a risk that excessive trading can interfere with one’s daily life, so please think it over carefully and proceed with caution. Related Viral horror game features creepy anime girl that hunts you down with killer traps Jujutsu Kaisen threatens $65,000 fine & prison time for Execution piracy Fanum reveals heart attack health scare after streaming hiatus Article continues after ad The story contains depictions of foreign forex brokers and high leverage trading. Furthermore, when actually engaging in trading, read all pre-contractual disclosure documents carefully, understand their contents, and then decide whether to engage in FX trading at your own risk and discretion.” Crunchyroll As you can imagine, this disclaimer has made quite a splash amongst the anime community, and many have praised the show for tackling the risks that come with trading. Article continues after ad “Man, you know this episode is gonna be good when they open up with a disclaimer and a warning about Forex trading, a bit similar to the warnings I get from a trading app,” wrote one commenter. Article continues after ad “As someone who trades exactly what Kurumi trades in this episode, I must say that this episode is absolute perfection, and probably the most true-to-real-life feel in anime of anything where I’ve had firsthand experience,” explained another. The first episode of FX Fighter Kurumi-chan aired on October 1 and is currently streaming on Crunchyroll . title: McDonald’s reveals Blue Lock menu with multiple Nagi Bao Burgers and 32-page mini mangas
summary: McDonald’s is bringing Blue Lock to its menu with three Nagi Bao Burgers, a bright blue Sprite and a KitKat White Matcha McFlurry.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment Food McDonald’s reveals Blue Lock menu with multiple Nagi Bao Burgers and 32-page mini mangas by Michael Gwilliam Published: Sep 23, 2026, 13:20 Save for later Save for later McDonald's Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News McDonald’s is bringing Blue Lock to its menu with three Nagi Bao Burgers, a bright blue Sprite and a KitKat White Matcha McFlurry. The collaboration is inspired by Blue Lock Episode Nagi, the soccer manga spinoff centered on Seishiro Nagi. It launched at McDonald’s restaurants in France on September 22 and is scheduled to run through October 26. The company has not announced a launch outside France. The Nagi Bao Burger comes in beef, crispy chicken, and breaded fish versions. Each uses a soft, white bao-style bun topped with black sesame seeds, plus cheddar, carrots, lettuce, cabbage, and a soy-based umami sauce. The beef option has two patties. Article continues after ad The drink is a sugar-free, passion fruit-flavored Sprite colored blue with spirulina extract. title: Dragon Ball Goku voice actor furious at “unforgivable” AI videos using her voice: “It has no heart”
summary: Dragon Ball voice actress Masako Nozawa has slammed AI-generated videos using her voice without permission.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Dragon Ball Goku voice actor furious at “unforgivable” AI videos using her voice: “It has no heart” by Michael Gwilliam Published: Oct 15, 2026, 17:53 Save for later Save for later NHK/Toei Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Dragon Ball voice actress Masako Nozawa has slammed AI-generated videos using her voice without permission, calling the practice “unforgivable” and comparing it to theft. The 89-year-old Japanese actress has voiced Goku since Dragon Ball debuted in 1986, also portraying characters including Gohan and Goten throughout the franchise. Her decades of work have earned her widespread recognition, with Nozawa becoming the first voice actor to receive one of Japan’s highest cultural honors in 2025. However, the Dragon Ball legend is now speaking out against the growing use of artificial intelligence to recreate her performances without consent. Article continues after ad Crunchyroll Goku voice actress blasts AI videos for stealing her voice Speaking to Japanese broadcaster NHK , Nozawa expressed her frustration with AI-generated videos that imitate her voice, arguing that the technology cannot replicate the emotion behind her performances. “It has no heart,” she said, according to a translation shared by Dragon Ball Hype. “It might even be a perfect copy. But it has no heart, does it? Without heart, it’s no good, whatever the role. Even a voice that’s only crying is different when you cry with real feeling. That’s what I believe.” Article continues after ad Article continues after ad “This is not my voice. Using it without permission is unforgivable. It’s the same as theft, and it makes me angry,” she added. Nozawa stressed that her voice and acting belong to her, arguing that anyone looking to recreate or use her performances should seek permission first. Masako Nozawa comments on the use of generative AI in voice acting: "I can't forgive using it without asking. I want people to follow the rules.” After watching AI videos of her voice: "This is not my voice. Using it without asking is unforgivable. It's the same as stealing,… pic.twitter.com/o3w5F1rBeK — Hype (@DbsHype) October 15, 2026 The comments came as the Japan Actors Union, which represents roughly 2,600 actors and voice performers, announced new guidelines on October 15 aimed at protecting performers from unauthorized AI voice cloning. Related Genshin Impact dev wins over $100K after AI company cloned character voices Evangelion star calls for Japanese government help over “heartbreaking” AI voice cloning Goku voice actor accuses popular Dragon Ball YouTuber of using AI to fake voices Article continues after ad The guidelines call for performers to give consent before their voices are used to train AI models, generate new recordings, or appear in published content. They also outline appropriate compensation and protections against unauthorized use. Nozawa is not entirely opposed to the technology, however. In a video message supporting the announcement, she expressed excitement about AI’s potential while criticizing those using performers’ voices without permission. She’s far from the only anime star raising concerns about the growing technology. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad In August 2026, Evangelion voice actress Megumi Ogata called AI voice cloning “heartbreaking” and urged Japan’s government to intervene. Meanwhile, Goku’s English voice actor Sean Schemmel previously accused a popular Dragon Ball YouTuber of using AI to imitate his voice , although the creator denied the allegations and insisted the impressions were entirely his own. With AI-generated anime content becoming increasingly widespread, Nozawa’s comments highlight the growing concerns among voice actors about losing control of the characters and performances they’ve spent decades bringing to life. title: Starbucks Japan unveils new Potato Soupuccino that’s said to be more than just soup
summary: New “self-care soup” blurs the line between soup and cappuccino. With temperatures starting to dip in Japan, Starbucks is adding warmth to its menu with an all-new Soupuccino. First introduced in 2025, the Soupuccino blurs the line between soup and cappuccino by adding a frothy, fluffy foam to the mix, creating a light and airy […]
details: New “self-care soup” blurs the line between soup and cappuccino. With temperatures starting to dip in Japan, Starbucks is adding warmth to its menu with an all-new Soupuccino . First introduced in 2025, the Soupuccino blurs the line between soup and cappuccino by adding a frothy, fluffy foam to the mix, creating a light and airy soup that looks great and is fun and easy to sip on. ▼ Now, after serving up the Soupuccino in truffle and pumpkin flavours, Starbucks is giving us an all-new flavour: Potato . This new ingredient is said to add extra heartiness to the Soupuccino, with milk providing a gentle creaminess for a delicious “ self-care soup ”. The concept of “self-care” is one that the chain is actively using to promote the Soupuccino, with Starbucks saying it offers an opportunity for you to take care of yourself even during a busy day . Whether it’s a morning cup on a chilly day, a light snack during a work break, or a moment to unwind in the evening, Starbucks is encouraging customers to wrap both hands around the warm cup and enjoy “a gentle flavour encased in fluffy foam”. The Potato Soupuccino is richly layered, replicating the fluffy, oven-baked texture and taste of potatoes as the main element. The first sip imparts the deep, savoury flavour of caramelised onions, followed by subtle hints of sweet vegetables. The gentle sweetness and buttery smoothness of potatoes brings everything together, creating a comforting flavour that’s perfect for the colder months. ▼ As you drink the soup, the flavours blend together, becoming even richer, while roasted almonds on top add crunch and a nutty accent. Each cup is finished by a barista who steams the milk individually, giving the soup a smooth layer of foam, similar to a cappuccino, for a distinctive drinking experience. Another appealing feature is the option to pay a little extra to switch the milk to suit your personal tastes – switching to almond milk, for instance, complements the fragrant roasted almonds, further enhancing the taste and texture of the potato. The Potato Soupuccino will be priced from 491 yen (US$3.11) for a Short and 530 yen for a Tall. According to Starbucks, the new release is more than just a soup – it’s a gesture of self-care that’s perfectly timed for the end of the year, when you may find yourself putting your own needs last as you get caught up in work, studies and household chores. The idea of taking a comforting break with a warm cup of soup in hand is one we can certainly get on board with, and we’ll definitely be trying it when it’s released for a limited time starting 13 November. title: Katsuya takes perhaps a little too much liberty with its take on a Niigata soul food
summary: We might be just a little bit saucy about this double-sauced version of a classic local specialty dish. Way back in 1931, a restaurant called Komatsu Parlor in Nagaoka, Niigata Prefecture served up a novel dish that was dubbed Western-style katsudon, in which tonkatsu (deep-fried pork cutlet) was placed on top of a bed of […]
details: We might be just a little bit saucy about this double-sauced version of a classic local specialty dish. Way back in 1931, a restaurant called Komatsu Parlor in Nagaoka, Niigata Prefecture served up a novel dish that was dubbed Western-style katsudon , in which tonkatsu (deep-fried pork cutlet) was placed on top of a bed of rice and topped with a thick, Western-style sauce, usually with either a ketchup or a demi-glace base. Not only was it tasty but it had an elegant, refined appearance, and it quickly became known as a popular “soul food” of the area. Fast forward to the present, and modern tonkatsu and katsudon chain Katsuya released a limited-time menu item on November 6 for Aigake Western-Style Katsu Rice (869 yen/US$5.48). This dish is said to take inspiration from Nagaoka’s specialty dish while putting its own unique Katsuya spin on it…perhaps a little too much of a spin, in fact. Nevertheless, devoted fans of Katsuya that we are , we wanted to check it out for ourselves and headed to our local branch. We were particularly curious about whether the sauce would be the ketchup type or demi-glace type. When our order arrived in front of us, we were a little bit shocked at the contents. ▼ It turns out that it had both. The deep-fried pork loin was cut into six chunks, half of which were covered in a Japanese “aurora sauce” concoction of ketchup and Kewpie mayo… …while the other half were drenched in a demi-glace sauce. In other words, it was a best-of-both-worlds kind of deal. Some skeptics may think it’s unnecessary to combine both types on a single plate, but at least this way we could sample two different versions of the same dish. The tonkatsu was resting on a small bed of white rice and on the side was also the typical accompaniment of shaved cabbage along with Japanese-style “Napolitan” ketchup spaghetti and a sunny-side-up fried egg. The plate as a whole looked a little bit busy, like a slightly chaotic fried food theme park. We started our meal with the demi-glace side of the plate. It was strange how the addition of a sauce like this could elevate the ordinary tonkatsu into a somehow gourmet flavor. On the other hand, while the aurora sauce on its own had a strong, sour kick–to the point where we tasted the same burst of acidity as with pickled ume–it evened out splendidly on top of the meat. This blended sauce might not be for everyone, but we actually preferred it to the demi-glace version. Moving on, the pasta was springer than we initially thought and had that classic Napolitan taste with bits of bacon. Its flavor was further enhanced by its the seeping egg yolk neighbor. There was also enough sauce beginning to pool on the plate that we were able to pour it over the cabbage and turn over a new leaf. All in all, while we enjoyed the new Aigake Western-Style Katsu Rice dish, we have to wonder if all of Katsuya’s extreme modifications to its originator in Niigata are completely necessary. The plate also lacked a little bit of the visual impact of other recent Katsuya creations that we’ve tried . In any case, we’ll continue searching for more local takes on the tasty, deep-fried dish that have been around for decades . summary: While the rest of the world is scraping away at their yogurt containers, we’re keeping things cultured with our new favorite spoon. details: While the rest of the world is scraping away at their yogurt containers, we’re keeping things cultured with our new favorite spoon. In today’s installment of Japanese kitchen gadgets that just make everything easier , we’d like to present a spoon –not just any spoon, but a magical spoon that specializes in scooping up every last bit of your yogurt. OK, while we can’t guarantee that it’s actually imbued with magic, the spoon produced by Japanese houseware brand Marna sure seems to have some kind of mystical ability. We’d caught wind of it through the grapevine and decided to test it out for ourselves. Its simple design involves a pliable tip made of silicone and a sturdy blue handle. ▼ We’ve got a good gut feeling about this one. From a side view, it’s easy to see how the handle curves into an elegant angle at the tip. Let’s test it out in action. Would it really make a difference in how we eat yogurt now and forevermore? As we began eating, we noticed immediately how little effort it took to perfectly scour the inside of the container from all angles. It felt like a mini spatula in this sense, also being quieter than a regular metal spoon. Amazingly, there was almost no yogurt left clinging to the bottom or the sides of the cup once we had finished, despite not making any extra effort to scrape at the very end. We next decided to hold a mini controlled experiment by eating one more of the exact same kind of yogurt using a regular metal spoon to compare the results. We tried eating it as gracefully as possible but there was still some yogurt left at the bottom of the cup at the end. It seems that the fixed shape of the metal tip in this case prevented us from getting it all. In conclusion, the spoon served its purpose incredibly well, living up to its promise of not wasting any yogurt with minimal effort. ▼ Yogurt container after using a regular metal spoon (left) and the special yogurt spoon (right) In a fun collaboration, Marna also sells a version of the spoon together with Hiroshima-based company Chichiyasu , the first company in Japan to begin selling yogurt in 1917. Marna’s yogurt spoon retails for 594 yen (US$3.75) and can be ordered through Marna’s official site or Rakuten Japan . While we never knew what we had been missing all of these years, it’s going to be hard to go back to eating yogurt any other way now. title: Pokémon card game’s expansion features art from Fist of the North Star creator
summary: Tetsuo Hara shows he can draw for both blood-soaked martial arts action and Pokémon. The Pokémon Trading Card Game pumps out way too many cards for one single illustrator to handle all of them, and being approached by the Pokémon Company to draw one can be a major feather in the cap of upcoming artists […]
details: Tetsuo Hara shows he can draw for both blood-soaked martial arts action and Pokémon . The Pokémon Trading Card Game pumps out way too many cards for one single illustrator to handle all of them, and being approached by the Pokémon Company to draw one can be a major feather in the cap of upcoming artists with a talent for drawing cute and cuddly critters…but it turns out it can also be an appealing project for legendary veterans of drawing ultra-violent, extra-macho manga series too. The game’s new Hado Seeker/Aura Seeker expansion packs (pictured above) are set to go on sale soon in Japan, and among the cards that could be waiting inside packs is one featuring Crasher Wake , the Pastoria City Gym Leader who first appeared in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl. The SAR (“special art rare”) version of the Crasher’s Passion card shows off an especially high level of detail on the character’s muscles, which makes sense once you know that it was drawn by none other than Tetsuo Hara, creator and artist of Fist of the North Star! Hara, who began drawing his post-apocalyptic marital arts saga in 1983, brings his distinct aesthetic of heavy shadowing to convey the mass of characters’ muscles, plus a whole lot of fist-shaped after images to represent rapid punch flurries, to the artwork. “Crasher is a pro wrestler, so I thought a lot about how best to show his toughness and physique,” the artist says. “I always want to pursue a sense of realism in my artwork, so I have to take into consideration how stylized I can get. At first, I was planning to draw Crashed with even bigger muscles, but after considering how that would or wouldn’t align with fans’ perception of the character, I ended up toning it down.” For the illustration’s layout, Hara says he wanted Crasher to be up in a wrestling ring, in order to create a powerful presence, but drawing him from that angle ran the risk of making his face look tiny, so he decided to have the character angled to be looking down from on high. This also allowed him to add in a few of the ring’s overhead lights in a stealthy homage to the constellation-motif that appears in Fist of the North Star . Hara also says that once he started adding after-images of Crasher’s punches, he realized the composition needed more and more, so many that he found himself thinking “Maybe I shouldn’t have done this” because of all the extra work he’d created for himself, but in the end it seems like a pretty safe bet that most fans are going to be very satisfied with how things turned out. For those wanting a closer look, the original artwork for the card will be on display at the Pokémon Card Station specialty shop attached to the Pokémon Center Ikebukuro store in Tokyo from November 30 to January 11 . This actually isn’t Hara’s first time to lend his talents to the Pokémon Trading Card Game . In 2024, he drew artwork for a special Palafin card that was part of the Terastal Fest Ex, which also featured an homage to Fist of the North Star protagonist Kenshiro’s iconic Hundred Crack Fist attack. Hara says that there’s a unique challenge in balancing his personal artistic sensibilities with the atmosphere of the Pokémon world, but that he’s enjoyed finding a way to blend the two, and the experience he acquired working on the Palafin card made the process of creating the Crasher one smoother, so hopefully there’ll be more Pokémon projects for him in the future. For the time being, though, the Hado Seeker expansion packs are scheduled to go on sale in Japan on November 27 . title: Forza Horizon 6 pone en la mira a las waifus: hasta unos ojos entrecerrados pueden ser un problema
summary: Forza Horizon 6 genera polémica por eliminar diseños de anime y sancionar a cientos de jugadores, incluso por pinturas privadas con personajes sugerentes.
details: Cultura Otaku Forza Horizon 6 pone en la mira a las waifus: hasta unos ojos entrecerrados pueden ser un problema El juego está sancionando diseños de anime, incluso privados, y ya son cientos los usuarios afectados. Ryo hace 1 hora 2 Comentarios ADS Resulta bastante irónico que un videojuego de carreras ambientado en Japón termine teniendo problemas con una de las costumbres más reconocibles de su cultura automovilística. Los creadores de Forza Horizon 6 están eliminando diseños de vehículos decorados con personajes de anime y sancionando a sus autores por considerarlos demasiado sugerentes. Lo más curioso es que, según las explicaciones de los responsables, unos ojos entrecerrados, labios ligeramente abiertos o determinada ropa pueden influir en la decisión de censurar una ilustración . La controversia comenzó a tomar fuerza durante septiembre, cuando varios jugadores japoneses denunciaron que sus creaciones habían desaparecido del videojuego. Se trataba principalmente de los llamados itasha , automóviles personalizados con ilustraciones de personajes de anime, manga y videojuegos, una práctica que tiene bastante popularidad en Japón y que lleva años formando parte de la comunidad de Forza . Ante las quejas, Playground Games publicó el pasado 30 de octubre un comunicado en sus redes sociales chinas para explicar los criterios de moderación. Según la compañía, los diseños con expresiones faciales sexualmente sugerentes, ropa provocativa o poses que destaquen determinadas partes del cuerpo pueden considerarse inapropiados, aunque no muestren desnudos. Eso sí, el estudio aclaró que no se trata de prohibir automáticamente cualquier personaje atractivo o con poca ropa. Por ejemplo, una ilustración de alguien usando bikini en la playa podría ser aceptable si el contexto, la postura y la composición no buscan transmitir una intención sexual. El problema, según los responsables, está en la combinación de elementos y no necesariamente en uno solo. Ni siquiera los diseños privados están completamente a salvo Otra de las cosas que más sorprendió a los jugadores fue descubrir que las reglas también se aplican a diseños que nunca fueron compartidos públicamente . La compañía explicó que, aunque una pintura permanezca sin publicar, otros usuarios podrían verla si el creador la utiliza en su automóvil durante una partida. Por esa razón, todos los diseños deben respetar las clasificaciones por edades del videojuego. Mientras que en Japón Forza Horizon 6 está clasificado para mayores de 12 años, en otras regiones tiene categorías que permiten jugar a públicos más jóvenes. El estudio sostiene que las creaciones de los usuarios deben cumplir con los criterios apropiados para esas audiencias. En cuanto al alcance de las sanciones, la compañía compartió algunas cifras para defender su sistema de moderación. Durante el último mes se habían creado más de 12.5 millones de contenidos personalizados y recibido aproximadamente 21,900 denuncias. De ellas, solamente el 3 por ciento terminaron en medidas disciplinarias que afectaron a menos de 700 usuarios . La mayoría recibió advertencias o suspensiones temporales, mientras que alrededor de 50 cuentas fueron suspendidas permanentemente por diseños que, según el estudio, contenían desnudos explícitos. Los responsables también aseguraron que cada denuncia es examinada por moderadores humanos y que recibir muchas quejas sobre una misma creación no hace que esta sea castigada automáticamente. Los jugadores japoneses no quedaron convencidos Sin embargo, estas explicaciones no lograron terminar con las críticas. Varios creadores consideran que las reglas sobre expresiones sugerentes son demasiado ambiguas y temen perder sus trabajos por ilustraciones que no consideran inapropiadas. También se han reportado eliminaciones de diseños que ni siquiera incluían personajes de anime, sino únicamente logotipos relacionados con automóviles. Otro detalle que causó molestia fue que la explicación más específica se publicara inicialmente para la comunidad china, semanas después de que comenzaran las denuncias en Japón. Para empeorar las cosas, el comunicado del 30 de octubre desapareció poco después de su publicación , aunque su contenido ya había sido traducido y compartido entre los jugadores. Por ahora, Playground Games mantiene que las ilustraciones de anime no están prohibidas por sí mismas, pero que deben cumplir con las normas de contenido del videojuego. Mientras tanto, los aficionados a los itasha siguen cuestionando dónde está exactamente la línea entre un diseño perfectamente aceptable y uno que podría costarles su cuenta. ¿Crees que unos ojos entrecerrados y labios ligeramente abiertos son suficientes para considerar provocativa a una waifu, o Forza Horizon 6 está llevando demasiado lejos sus reglas de moderación? title: YouTube banea a una seiyuu por Azur Lane, ¡el videojuego donde ella misma trabaja!
summary: YouTube eliminó el canal de Hinata Yuka, actriz de voz de Azur Lane, con 250,000 suscriptores. La seiyuu denunció un posible error de moderación.
details: Cultura Otaku YouTube banea a una seiyuu por Azur Lane, ¡el videojuego donde ella misma trabaja! Hinata Yuka perdió un canal con 250,000 suscriptores y más de 20 millones de vistas tras mostrar contenido del juego. Aiko hace 1 hora 1 Comentarios ADS Imagínate trabajar como actriz de voz en un videojuego, transmitirlo para tus seguidores y terminar perdiendo tu canal de YouTube por mostrar sus personajes. Pues algo así le ocurrió a Hinata Yuka , una seiyuu japonesa (famosa por prestar su voz para series de anime para adultos como Kaede to Suzu y también a juegos eroge) que anunció que la plataforma eliminó su canal de aproximadamente 250,000 suscriptores por supuestas infracciones relacionadas con contenido sexual. Lo curioso es que la artista atribuye el problema a sus transmisiones de Azur Lane , un videojuego donde ella misma interpreta a uno de los personajes. La situación comenzó a complicarse durante septiembre, cuando Hinata realizó una transmisión dedicada a los nuevos atuendos de Azur Lane . La actriz presta su voz a Golden Hind y decidió mostrar uno de los vestuarios recientemente incorporados para su personaje. Sin embargo, el archivo de aquella transmisión terminó siendo eliminado por YouTube y, posteriormente, también desaparecieron algunos fragmentos que había publicado. El pasado 25 de octubre, la actriz reveló que había recibido una nueva restricción que le impedía publicar contenido durante dos semanas. En ese momento todavía podía bromear sobre la situación, pues su canal seguía funcionando. Pero apenas tres días después, el 28 de octubre, recibió una noticia mucho peor: YouTube había eliminado completamente su cuenta . De acuerdo con las capturas compartidas por la propia artista, la plataforma justificó la medida por supuestas violaciones de sus políticas sobre desnudez y contenido sexual. Sin embargo, Hinata considera que se trata de un error del sistema de moderación automática , pues las imágenes cuestionadas pertenecían al propio videojuego y mostraban vestuarios disponibles oficialmente para los jugadores. La seiyuu presentó una apelación, pero fue rechazada. Posteriormente, contactó públicamente a la cuenta de asistencia de YouTube para solicitar que un empleado revisara manualmente su caso , argumentando que la inteligencia artificial había confundido las ilustraciones de Azur Lane con contenido prohibido. El 30 de octubre informó que había recibido otra respuesta indicando que recuperar su canal sería difícil. Y no estamos hablando precisamente de una cuenta pequeña. Según las estadísticas recopiladas por Yutura, el canal había sido creado en mayo de 2018 y acumulaba más de 20.6 millones de reproducciones y 369 videos . Además de sus transmisiones de videojuegos, Hinata publicaba contenido ASMR, interpretaciones de voz y canciones originales, por lo que el cierre también significó perder años de trabajo y recuerdos compartidos con sus seguidores. Aunque la situación la dejó bastante desanimada, la actriz aseguró que no se arrepiente de haber transmitido Azur Lane ni de los demás contenidos que decidió compartir. Por ahora, planea continuar sus actividades mediante las plataformas japonesas Ci-en y Niconico, mientras mantiene la esperanza de recuperar algún día su espacio en YouTube. Cabe aclarar que, aunque Hinata atribuye el cierre a un error de moderación relacionado con el videojuego, YouTube no ha confirmado públicamente que una inteligencia artificial haya provocado la sanción . Tampoco se ha detallado cuáles fueron todas las publicaciones consideradas infractoras. ¿Crees que YouTube debería revisar manualmente estos casos antes de eliminar canales con años de actividad, especialmente cuando las imágenes cuestionadas pertenecen a un videojuego que se distribuye oficialmente? title: Las Vtubers de Yugiri High School cancelan su primer gran festival y crece la polémica contra viviON
summary: Yugiri High School canceló su primer gran festival tras la suspensión indefinida de Amarasu Terasu, mientras crecen las críticas contra viviON.
details: Cultura Otaku Las Vtubers de Yugiri High School cancelan su primer gran festival y crece la polémica contra viviON La suspensión de Amarasu Terasu provocó la cancelación del evento apenas dos días antes de su inicio. Mirukaru hace 31 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Los fanáticos de Yugiri High School estaban a punto de disfrutar del primer gran festival de sus VTubers favoritas, pero los planes terminaron derrumbándose apenas dos días antes del evento. La compañía viviON anunció la cancelación del festival virtual del grupo después de suspender indefinidamente las actividades de Amarasu Terasu, una de sus cinco integrantes. Y para complicar todavía más las cosas, la decisión llegó poco después de que las propias chicas hablaran públicamente sobre los problemas que habían enfrentado con su administración. El festival estaba programado para celebrarse del 31 de octubre al 2 de noviembre de 2026 a través del canal oficial de YouTube. Se trataba de la primera gran actividad conjunta desde la apertura de dicho canal, con presentaciones musicales, videos especiales y diferentes actividades preparadas por las cinco integrantes. Sin embargo, el 28 de octubre, viviON anunció que Amarasu Terasu quedaría suspendida por tiempo indefinido mientras la empresa investigaba diversas declaraciones y comportamientos registrados durante sus transmisiones. La compañía explicó que necesitaba verificar los hechos y que no podía ofrecer detalles adicionales debido a cuestiones contractuales. Como parte de las medidas, la agencia también ocultó el archivo de una transmisión realizada ese mismo día y solicitó que los usuarios evitaran compartir fragmentos de su contenido. Hasta el momento, no se ha especificado públicamente qué declaraciones concretas motivaron la suspensión ni cuándo podría regresar la VTuber. Lo que más llamó la atención de los seguidores fue que, apenas unos días antes, las cinco integrantes habían hablado sobre las dificultades que enfrentaron durante los preparativos de su debut . El 24 de octubre participaron en una transmisión donde cuestionaron la falta de apoyo y organización que, según sus relatos, experimentaron durante la gestión de su anterior productor. Entre las situaciones mencionadas se encontraban proyectos que no avanzaban como esperaban, problemas para organizar actividades conjuntas y la sensación de tener que resolver por su cuenta diferentes aspectos de su trabajo. También reconocieron que algunas condiciones habían comenzado a mejorar con los cambios administrativos. Por esa razón, la suspensión de Amarasu provocó nuevas críticas contra viviON. Algunos seguidores sospecharon que la decisión podría estar relacionada con las declaraciones sobre los problemas internos de la compañía. Sin embargo, esa relación no ha sido confirmada , y la empresa tampoco ha identificado públicamente cuáles fueron los comentarios que considera problemáticos. El 29 de octubre llegó el segundo golpe. La administración explicó que el festival había sido preparado específicamente para contar con las cinco integrantes y que, ante la ausencia de Amarasu, no podrían ofrecer el evento en las condiciones prometidas. Por ello, decidieron cancelarlo por completo y ofrecieron disculpas a quienes esperaban las actividades. La controversia resulta todavía más delicada porque Yugiri High School es un grupo hermano de Aogiri High School , otra agrupación de VTubers administrada por la misma compañía que recientemente también enfrentó problemas de organización. En septiembre, un concierto de aniversario de Chiyoura Chomi tuvo que posponerse apenas dos días antes de su celebración. Posteriormente, la empresa reconoció distintas fallas administrativas y anunció una reorganización interna. Como parte de ese proceso, también canceló un festival musical de Aogiri High School previsto para diciembre . Así, dos agrupaciones de la misma compañía terminaron perdiendo importantes eventos en cuestión de semanas. Mientras viviON asegura que trabaja para mejorar las condiciones de sus talentos, los seguidores de Yugiri High School continúan esperando una explicación más clara sobre el futuro de Amarasu Terasu y las actividades del grupo. ¿Crees que viviON hizo bien en cancelar el festival para no presentarlo sin una de sus integrantes, o debería haber encontrado una manera de realizarlo con las otras cuatro VTubers? title: La seiyuu Hazuki Tanda se disfrazó de Shaun the Sheep y terminó acusada de racismo
summary: La seiyuu Hazuki Tanda recibió acusaciones de racismo por su disfraz de Shaun the Sheep. Su maquillaje de Halloween dividió a los usuarios de redes sociales.
details: Cultura Otaku La seiyuu Hazuki Tanda se disfrazó de Shaun the Sheep y terminó acusada de racismo La seiyuu de D4DJ se pintó el rostro de negro para Halloween y provocó una discusión internacional. Kenji hace 33 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Uno pensaría que disfrazarse de una oveja para Halloween sería una de las decisiones menos problemáticas del mundo, pero parece que internet siempre encuentra una manera de sorprendernos. La actriz de voz japonesa Hazuki Tanda , conocida por su participación en BanG Dream! y D4DJ , terminó envuelta en una controversia internacional después de publicar fotografías de su disfraz de Shaun the Sheep . ¿El problema? Se pintó el rostro de negro para recrear al personaje , algo que varios usuarios extranjeros interpretaron como una representación racista. Todo comenzó el pasado 31 de octubre, cuando la seiyuu compartió en X varias fotografías acompañadas de un sencillo saludo de Halloween. Para recrear a Shaun, el protagonista de la popular serie británica de animación, utilizó un traje cubierto de material blanco que simulaba lana, ropa negra y maquillaje oscuro en el rostro, dejando el contorno de los ojos de color blanco. Además, posó sosteniendo un plátano y algunas verduras , incluyendo un puerro. La publicación también incluía una imagen del personaje original para dejar claro cuál era la inspiración de su disfraz. Inicialmente, muchos seguidores japoneses celebraron la creatividad de la actriz y lo divertido que resultaba verla convertida en la famosa oveja. Sin embargo, cuando las fotografías comenzaron a circular fuera de Japón, las reacciones cambiaron. Varios usuarios acusaron a Tanda de recurrir al blackface , una práctica históricamente asociada con representaciones racistas de personas negras. Las críticas se intensificaron por la presencia del plátano, debido a que esta fruta también ha sido utilizada en insultos y estereotipos raciales. La controversia provocó una discusión entre usuarios de diferentes países. Mientras algunos consideraban que pintarse el rostro de negro era inapropiado independientemente del personaje representado, otros recordaron un detalle bastante evidente: Shaun es una oveja que tiene la cara y las patas negras . Desde esa perspectiva, la actriz simplemente estaba intentando reproducir su apariencia original. Numerosos usuarios japoneses defendieron a Tanda y cuestionaron que el maquillaje pudiera interpretarse automáticamente como una burla racial. También hubo comentarios de seguidores internacionales que consideraban injustas las acusaciones, especialmente porque las fotografías mostraban claramente al personaje que estaba recreando. La discusión, sin embargo, tiene un trasfondo histórico. El blackface se popularizó durante el siglo XIX en espectáculos estadounidenses donde artistas blancos se maquillaban para caricaturizar a las personas negras, reforzando estereotipos discriminatorios. Por eso, algunos usuarios consideraron ofensiva la combinación de maquillaje oscuro, material parecido al algodón y un plátano, aunque esos elementos tuvieran otra explicación dentro del disfraz. La controversia llegó incluso a la prensa japonesa. En una entrevista publicada por NEWS Post Seven , la profesora Fumiko Sakashita, especialista en historia y cultura afroestadounidense de la Universidad Sofía, explicó que el caso de Tanda no necesariamente merece las mismas críticas , puesto que estaba representando a una oveja de rostro negro. No obstante, también consideró importante reflexionar sobre cuándo es realmente necesario modificar el color de la piel para interpretar a un personaje. Por ahora, Hazuki Tanda no ha publicado una explicación formal sobre las acusaciones , y su mensaje original de Halloween no hacía ninguna referencia a cuestiones raciales. Lo que comenzó como una publicación para mostrar un disfraz terminó convirtiéndose en una discusión sobre las diferencias culturales y la manera en que una misma imagen puede interpretarse de formas muy distintas. ¿Crees que el contexto de estar disfrazada de Shaun the Sheep debería ser suficiente para descartar las acusaciones, o consideras que Tanda pudo haber recreado al personaje de otra manera? title: One Piece brings back rare $400 East Blue and Nami Log Pose watches

details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment One Piece brings back rare $400 East Blue and Nami Log Pose watches by James Busby Published: Sep 15, 2026, 09:57 Save for later Save for later Tendence Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News One Piece is bringing back two limited-edition watches that sold out when they launched in 2018, including one that recreates Nami’s iconic Log Pose. Following hot on the heels of One Piece’s Timberland and Nike collab , the popular anime is now teaming up with Swiss watch brand Tendence. Article continues after ad The clock face also features the Straw Hats’ signature Jolly Roger and giant rose-gold numbers, while the silicone straps come in soft beige. Article continues after ad 1 of 4 Its East Blue counterpart takes a grander approach to One Piece’s seafaring world, placing a map beneath Luffy’s pirate ship’s wheel. Just like the compass on Nami’s Log Pose watch, the ship wheel also moves with the wearer’s wrist. The site also mentions that the red-colored section of the wheel can be used to predict the wearer’s lucky direction for the day. If you follow it, maybe you’ll find your own Devil Fruit/One Piece, or just get hopelessly lost (who really knows?) title: Clannad and Angel Beats creator opts against active cancer treatment to focus on work
summary: The writer and composer behind Clannad, Angel Beats, and Heaven Burns Red has been diagnosed with throat cancer and has chosen to focus on palliative care so he can continue creating.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment Anime Clannad and Angel Beats creator opts against active cancer treatment to focus on work by James Busby Published: Oct 19, 2026, 12:59 Save for later Save for later VisualArts/Key Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News The creator behind Clannad and the anime series Angel Beats has been diagnosed with throat cancer and has chosen to focus on palliative care so he can continue creating. On October 19, Visual Arts, the company Maeda works for, confirmed that he is currently hospitalized after being diagnosed with throat cancer. After considering his condition and the outlook for treatment, Maeda has decided against active treatment to conserve his strength for his creative work. The company also shared an update on his contributions to Heaven Burns Red and a new music project, which he now hopes to complete more quickly following his diagnosis. Article continues after ad Clannad writer shares health update and plans for future projects In its official statement, Visual Arts said Maeda began experiencing throat discomfort in early spring. However, a subsequent medical examination found that the swelling and pain became more pronounced over the summer. “After careful consideration of his condition and the outlook for treatment, Maeda has chosen not to pursue active treatment and instead to focus on palliative care, wishing to conserve his strength and devote himself to his creative work,” the company said. Article continues after ad Maeda has already completed his assigned writing for Heaven Burns Red’s main story through the first half of Chapter 6. He has also finished all the major story elements that will carry the narrative through the chapter’s conclusion, along with the lyrics and composition for songs featured in its first half. Article continues after ad However, Visual Arts said the progression of his illness could prevent him from participating in the creation of other scenarios and songs. Amazon Maeda also worked on Angel Beats as a planner and writer, and composed the anime’s music. Alongside his work on the game, Maeda had been developing an original music project with plans to release new songs on YouTube over the long term. His diagnosis has prompted him to change that approach. “He felt that there was little time remaining in which he would be able to continue creating,” the statement said. Related Castlevania and Bloodstained developer Shutaro Ida dies aged 52 Kyedae might shave her head before cancer treatment and wants other streamers to join in Valorant community shows support following Kyedae’s cancer diagnosis Article continues after ad Maeda now plans to complete the songs currently in development as quickly as possible so they can reach fans. At his request, the finished works will be released on YouTube. Article continues after ad “Maeda is currently hospitalized, but even under these circumstances, he remains strongly determined to devote himself to creative work through to the very end,” the company said. “We would be grateful for your warm understanding and support of his wishes.” Fans wishing to send messages of encouragement can do so by using the email address at the bottom of the English statement . Visual Arts has also provided a postal address for letters, but has asked fans to refrain from sending gifts. The details can also be found via the statement linked above. title: Student sparks police investigation after bringing ‘Death Note’ book to school
summary: A Massachusetts student’s ‘Death Note’ notebook prompted a suspension and a real police investigation, with one parent demanding stronger action.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment Student sparks police investigation after bringing ‘Death Note’ book to school by Michael Gwilliam Published: Oct 12, 2026, 14:51 Save for later Save for later Netflix Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News A Massachusetts student’s ‘Death Note’ notebook prompted a suspension and a real police investigation, with one parent demanding stronger action despite officials finding no immediate threat. In Death Note , Light Yagami’s notebook attracts the attention of a mysterious detective known as L. At Chocksett Middle School in Sterling, a student’s version brought in local police. Administrators contacted officers on September 30 after discovering the notebook. Students had already been dismissed when police responded. Article continues after ad The student explained to staff it was connected to the manga and anime, in which Light uses a supernatural notebook to kill criminals by writing their names inside. Student suspended after Death Note concerns According to Boston.com , principal Tina Boss said investigators interviewed dozens of students and found no evidence the notebook was intended to threaten the school or any particular student. “Based on the information gathered, including dozens of student interviews and the investigation conducted by the Sterling Police Department, our multidisciplinary team has found no indication that the notebook or its contents were intended as a threat toward the school or any particular student,” she told the community. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad “The information indicates that the notebook was indeed connected to a television series and an inappropriate theme that has made its way into the school,” she added, further saying the book was from an anime with an “inappropriate theme.” Madhouse Police found no immediate threat and said they were not seeking criminal charges based on the available information. However, the explanation that it was inspired by Light’s fictional notebook did little to reassure parent Jen DiCandia. She said her daughter’s name appeared inside and challenged the student’s return following a three-day suspension. Related Teachers panic after finding student’s ‘Death Note’ at LeBron James’ I Promise school School suspends autistic 6-year-old for biting sandwich into shape of gun Rapper Fetty Wap sends flowers to principal suspended after his lyrics appeared in yearbook Article continues after ad “She deserves to feel safe in her classroom, every single day,” DiCandia wrote. The family has since retained an attorney, Sentinel & Enterprise reported . DiCandia said the students still shared three classes and called for them to be permanently separated at school. “My goal is for my daughter to attend school safely and continue her education without fear,” she said. “I don’t really care if it’s a joke, a video game, whatever. It’s not funny.” Article continues after ad Article continues after ad Death Note notebooks have a long history of causing trouble at school Ryuk’s notebook has inspired plenty of real-world imitations, and Sterling is far from the first school to investigate one. In September 2026, a 12-year-old in Florida was arrested after a ‘Death Note’ listing students and staff was found at Argyle Elementary School . Deputies said another student alerted a teacher after seeing the note being written. The teacher retrieved it from a trash can, and investigators arrested the student on a written-threat charge. Netflix In 2024, teachers and staff at LeBron James’ I Promise school in Akron, Ohio were left panicking after an instructor found a homemade ‘Death Note’ on the floor of a classroom Article continues after ad Back in 2008, two 12-year-olds in Alabama were arrested after authorities discovered a Death Note-inspired notebook containing students’ and school employees’ names. The boys reportedly told their principal it was a joke. In 2015, a Death Note-inspired list at a New Hampshire high school contained 17 names, alarming parents and prompting a school investigation. The notebooks lack the anime’s supernatural powers, but writing classmates’ names inside has repeatedly brought real consequences. title: Japan celebrates anime couple getting together after 28 years with trucks and a boat
summary: Two anime characters have finally become a couple after 28 years of “will they/won’t they” moments, and Japan is celebrating their long-awaited relationship with advertising trucks and a boat showcasing their romance.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Japan celebrates anime couple getting together after 28 years with trucks and a boat by James Busby Published: Oct 12, 2026, 13:18 Save for later Save for later TMS Entertainment Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Two anime characters have finally become a couple after 28 years of “will they/won’t they” moments, and Japan is celebrating their long-awaited relationship with advertising trucks and a boat showcasing their romance. Slow-burning relationships are nothing new for anime fans, just look at the likes of Naruto and Hinata. However, fans rarely have to wait nearly three decades for characters who clearly love one another to become Facebook official. For fans of Detective Conan, that’s exactly what has happened as one of the show’s longest-running romances has finally taken a major step forward. On October 10, Heiji Hattori and Kazuha Toyama officially became a couple after 28 long years of waiting. In fact, Kazuha first appeared in the anime in 1998, and ever since then, the pair have left viewers patiently waiting for their romance to blossom. Article continues after ad If you’ve seen any anime, chances are you’ve seen how painful it can be for characters to get to a stage where they can even hold hands or go in for that big first kiss. Combine this with the fact that it’s taken 28 years to reach this moment, and you have something that is on par with Ross and Rachel’s relationship from Friends, but just with even more waiting. Article continues after ad According to a translated report via Livedoor News , advertising trucks celebrating the pair are currently traveling through Osaka’s Umeda, Shinsaibashi, and Namba areas until October 17. Meanwhile, a boat carrying ads celebrating the couple will be cruising along the Dotonbori River from 4 pm each day until October 13. ╭━━━━━━━━━━━━━━╮ 祝！平次♡和葉 #茜色の千秋楽 お祝いアドクルーズ運航中⛴️ ╰━ｖ━━━━━━━━━━━━╯ 10/11(日)～10/13(火)まで 夕方4時から道頓堀川を運航中 あの戎橋も通ります🎉 「茜色の千秋楽（大楽）」は TVerで見逃し配信中🎬 pic.twitter.com/PijP1KXVo0 — アニメ名探偵コナン【公式】⚽️ (@conan_anime1000) October 11, 2026 While Detective Conan fans have been rejoicing over the long-awaited romance, Heiji’s voice actor, Ryo Horikawa, also reflected on how the confession finally unfolded after years of failed attempts. Article continues after ad Related Hatsune Miku takes over Tokyo Metro with themed train and hotel room 10 best romantic anime to watch this Valentine’s Day Jujutsu Kaisen is reuniting Gojo and Geto soon, and fans can’t keep calm Article continues after ad “At first, I imagined all sorts of ways he might confess. I wondered whether he would look Kazuha straight in the eyes and tell her he loved her,” he said. “But after so many failed attempts, his feelings just slipped out, and Kazuha happened to overhear him. It became something like, ‘Is that really true?’ followed by, ‘It’s true!’” Horikawa also had a message for his character: “Heiji Hattori, you lucky guy! Take good care of Kazuha. Oh, and Ryo Horikawa is rooting for the two of them too. After all, I’m Heiji.” Article continues after ad コナンのテーマソング聞こえると思ったら さすが大阪だ pic.twitter.com/Nb15nSzsYN — みく (@yummy102) October 11, 2026 Kazuha’s voice actor, Yuko Miyamura, was equally pleased to see the two characters finally become a couple. “Finally!! Heiji’s confession was a success, and their feelings for each other have finally been confirmed!” she said. “Everyone around them already knew they liked each other, but he had to go looking for a spectacular spot to rival Big Ben. Honestly, it took so long!” Article continues after ad Despite the decades that have passed for viewers, Miyamura noted that considerably less time has elapsed within the story. Article continues after ad Detective Conan fans in Japan can also relive the confession at Osaka’s Abeno Harukas, the real building that inspired its setting. Starting October 11, the Harukas 300 observation deck features footprints marking where the characters stood, alongside audio from the anime. An exclusive conversation never shown in the anime or manga will play in the elevator on the way down, which will reveal what Heiji and Kazuha said after the confession. title: SPY x FAMILY tendrá temporada 4 y otra película: Anya no descansará en 2027
summary: SPY x FAMILY anuncia su cuarta temporada y una segunda película para 2027. La familia Forger regresará con nuevas aventuras y una imagen promocional.
details: Anime SPY x FAMILY tendrá temporada 4 y otra película: Anya no descansará en 2027 La familia Forger regresará por partida doble en 2027 y ya tiene una primera imagen de su cuarta temporada. Yuna hace 35 minutos 0 Comentarios ADS Parece que Anya todavía tendrá que seguir soportando las misiones de su padre, las peligrosas habilidades culinarias de su madre y uno que otro examen escolar. Y es que los responsables de SPY x FAMILY anunciaron que la franquicia tendrá una cuarta temporada y una nueva película en 2027 , así que los seguidores podrán disfrutar de las aventuras de la familia Forger tanto en televisión como en los cines. La noticia se dio a conocer durante el evento especial SPY x FAMILY ANIME EXTRA MISSION II , celebrado este 8 de noviembre en Tokio. Allí se confirmó que la cuarta temporada comenzará sus emisiones en algún momento de 2027 , mientras que la segunda película de la franquicia llegará a los cines japoneses durante ese mismo año. Por ahora, ninguna de las dos producciones tiene una fecha exacta de estreno. El anuncio también llegó acompañado de una primera imagen promocional de la cuarta temporada , ilustrada por Satoshi Kadowaki, uno de los diseñadores de personajes del anime. En ella aparecen Loid, Yor, Anya y Bond caminando juntos por la ciudad, mientras diferentes periódicos y folletos vuelan a su alrededor. Y aunque a primera vista parece una escena bastante tranquila, los responsables adelantaron que los documentos que aparecen en la ilustración contienen pistas sobre los acontecimientos de la próxima temporada . Así que probablemente más de un fanático terminará examinando la imagen con lupa para intentar descubrir qué les espera a nuestros espías favoritos. SPY x FAMILY también prepara su segunda película La otra gran sorpresa fue la confirmación de una nueva película de SPY x FAMILY , que será la segunda producción cinematográfica de la franquicia. Sin embargo, todavía no se ha revelado su título, argumento ni equipo de producción, por lo que tendremos que esperar para saber si contará una aventura independiente o estará relacionada con los acontecimientos de la serie. Cabe recordar que la primera película, SPY x FAMILY Code: White , se estrenó en Japón en diciembre de 2023 y consiguió superar los 6,260 millones de yenes en recaudación dentro del país. Aquella aventura llevó a la familia Forger a unas vacaciones que, como era de esperarse, terminaron convirtiéndose en un auténtico desastre lleno de espías, enemigos y situaciones absurdas. Por otra parte, la tercera temporada del anime comenzó sus emisiones en octubre de 2025 y contó con 13 episodios. La serie continúa siguiendo a Loid Forger, un agente secreto que debe mantener una familia falsa para completar una importante misión. El problema es que su esposa Yor trabaja como asesina profesional y su hija adoptiva Anya puede leer la mente, aunque ninguno de los adultos conoce todos los secretos que se esconden bajo el mismo techo. La franquicia está basada en el manga de Tatsuya Endo , que comenzó a publicarse en marzo de 2019 a través de la plataforma Shonen Jump+ de Shueisha. La obra continúa en publicación y recientemente recibió su decimoctavo volumen recopilatorio, lanzado el 4 de noviembre en Japón. Además, ya supera 42 millones de copias en circulación , consolidándose como uno de los mayores éxitos del catálogo de la editorial. Por ahora, los responsables no han confirmado cuántos episodios tendrá la cuarta temporada ni qué plataformas transmitirán las nuevas producciones internacionalmente. Lo único seguro es que 2027 estará bastante ocupado para la familia Forger , que tendrá que compaginar sus problemas cotidianos con nuevas aventuras dentro y fuera de la pantalla grande. ¿Qué te emociona más: volver a ver las ocurrencias de Anya en una cuarta temporada o descubrir en qué nuevos problemas terminará metida la familia Forger durante su próxima película? title: Harajuku Himegoto House tendrá anime: buscaba asesinos y encontró un café rosa con un centauro
summary: Imagínate viajar hasta Tokio para convertirte en el asesino más poderoso del mundo y descubrir que tu nuevo lugar de entrenamiento parece una cafetería sacada...
details: Anime Harajuku Himegoto House tendrá anime: buscaba asesinos y encontró un café rosa con un centauro La nueva comedia de Plott presentó su primer tráiler, siete personajes y un elenco lleno de voces conocidas. Jin hace 30 segundos 0 Comentarios ADS Imagínate viajar hasta Tokio para convertirte en el asesino más poderoso del mundo y descubrir que tu nuevo lugar de entrenamiento parece una cafetería sacada de un anime de chicas lindas. Esa será la peculiar experiencia del protagonista de Harajuku Himegoto House , una nueva comedia original que tendrá un anime para televisión . La compañía Plott presentó oficialmente el proyecto con un primer tráiler, una imagen promocional y un elenco de voces que incluye a varios nombres bastante conocidos entre los fanáticos. La historia sigue a Mizuki Otokozawa , un muchacho de 19 años que sueña con convertirse en el asesino más fuerte del mundo. Convencido de que necesita aprender de los mejores, decide viajar al famoso barrio de Harajuku para encontrar un escondite donde supuestamente se reúnen algunos de los sicarios más legendarios de Japón. Sin embargo, cuando finalmente llega al lugar, descubre que el escondite es en realidad una cafetería completamente rosa , atendida por un grupo de personajes que parecen tener cualquier profesión menos la de asesinos. Entre ellos hay una gyaru que considera adorable prácticamente cualquier cosa, un joven vestido de lolita gótica y, por alguna razón, hasta un centauro. Por supuesto, Mizuki no entiende absolutamente nada. Él esperaba encontrar hombres intimidantes, armas peligrosas y un ambiente donde nadie pudiera confiar en nadie. En cambio, terminó rodeado de personas obsesionadas con las cosas lindas. Aunque, por lo visto, las apariencias engañan y todos ellos tienen habilidades bastante peligrosas . Harajuku Himegoto House reunirá a siete asesinos bastante peculiares El proyecto también confirmó a los siete integrantes de su elenco principal, incluyendo a Nobuhiko Okamoto, conocido por interpretar a Katsuki Bakugo en My Hero Academia , y Showtaro Morikubo, la voz de Shikamaru Nara en Naruto . Los personajes y sus respectivos actores son los siguientes: Mizuki Otokozawa: Yuya Hirose, el joven que sueña con convertirse en asesino. Mero Togariishi: Tetsuei Sumiya, una gyaru extremadamente optimista. Takara Rokurokusou: Sohei Horikane, un joven de estilo lolita gótica con una lengua bastante afilada. Kentaro Jinbayama: Masaru Yoshimura, un centauro que combina su apariencia elegante con habilidades de francotirador. Yuki Inubo: Takuma Nagatsuka, un muchacho pesimista que se encarga de la cocina. Hitoshi Haritsukekawara: Nobuhiko Okamoto, el extravagante gerente de la cafetería, que tiene 50 años y utiliza dos coletas. Sho Dogenzaka: Showtaro Morikubo, un hombre despreocupado que acumula una deuda prácticamente imposible de pagar. La primera ilustración promocional reúne a todos estos personajes con atuendos coloridos y diferentes accesorios que reflejan sus personalidades. Los diseños originales son obra de Akiakane , una ilustradora conocida por su estilo llamativo y su trabajo en proyectos musicales. El proyecto también tendrá canciones y eventos especiales Pero Harajuku Himegoto House no se limitará al anime. La producción forma parte de un proyecto multimedia desarrollado por Plott, Bandai Namco Music Live y Animate , que también contempla lanzamientos musicales y actividades con los actores de voz. De hecho, junto con el anuncio se publicó un video musical de Aisare Houdai!! Himegoto House///♡ , la primera canción del proyecto. La música estará bajo la supervisión del sello Lantis, mientras que Animate colaborará en las actividades promocionales. La presentación oficial también tuvo lugar durante el Animate Girls Festival 2026 , celebrado los días 7 y 8 de noviembre. En cuanto al anime, se confirmó que tendrá un formato de episodios cortos para televisión , aunque todavía no se ha revelado su fecha de estreno, el canal donde se transmitirá ni la duración exacta de sus capítulos. Por ahora, los responsables continuarán presentando información sobre los personajes y sus próximas actividades. ¿Te atreverías a entrar en una cafetería atendida por asesinos que parecen modelos de Harajuku, o saldrías corriendo en cuanto vieras que el centauro también sabe utilizar un rifle? title: Japanese hoodie for cat-loving gamers will keep you and your feline friend warm and fuzzy [Pics]
summary: Meowgaroo Hoodie 3’s clever design points mean you don’t have to choose between playing with your cat and playing your games. As the temperature gets lower and days get shorter, you might be thinking it’s time to bundle up and hunker down for the winter with warm clothing and fun games. Really, though, it’s time […]
details: Meowgaroo Hoodie 3’s clever design points mean you don’t have to choose between playing with your cat and playing your games . As the temperature gets lower and days get shorter, you might be thinking it’s time to bundle up and hunker down for the winter with warm clothing and fun games. Really, though, it’s time to bundle up and game on while simultaneously abiding by your cat’s whims . Thankfully, Japan’s Bibilab is conscious of the big-picture situation, and is prepared to offer a holistic solution with its newest creation, the Meowgaroo Hoodie 3 . Also known as the Nyangaru Parka 3 ( nyan being the Japanese equivalent of “meow” and “parka” being the more common way to refer to hoodies in Japan), the Meowgaroo Hoodie 3, as its name implies, is the latest generation of Bibilab’s cat-conscious roomwear line. Since cats are notoriously averse to compromising, the designers realize that when your feline friend wants to snuggle, there’s no way to dissuade it of the notion, and so the hoodie has a large marsupial-inspired pouch on the stomach for your cat to crawl inside of, keeping it cozily close and supported while keeping your hands free to work a game controller or keyboard/mouse setup . That’s far from the garment’s only clever design point, though. The decorative cat ears on the hood also stand out right away, but what you might miss at first glance is that the tips of the drawstring cords… …are actually fuzzy cat teasers , meaning that the hoodie has built-in cat toys, letting you quickly transition from playing games to playing with your cat without even having to get up from your seat. ▼ This is much better than staring at the “Please wait – online matchmaking in progress” screen. It also might not be immediately apparent why the Meowgaroo Hoodie 3 has such a spaciously sized chest pocket , given that chest pockets themselves are rare on sweatshirts. The reason is that it’s designed to be big enough to hold your smartphone… …so that you can record cute, candid videos of your cat while it’s in the pouch . Getting back to the pouch, it also has a drawstring that allows you to adjust the dimensions to keep your kitty as snugly secure as needed. Of course, as a space for your pet to cuddle, play, and possible snooze, the pouch is going to end up with cat hair inside it, but even that has been taken into account by the designers, who opted for a dual-layer construction that lets you unsnap and remove the lining for easier cleaning/washing . Bibilab is the same company who, back in the spring, created an entire work-from-home (or game-from-home) desk designed around the idea that your cat has no qualms about encroaching on your personal space, and the company says the Meowgaroo Hoodie 3 is part of its continuing efforts to transform the feeling of being harassed by your cat into an enjoyable time for pet and human alike . ▼ The integrated solution of Meowgaroo Hoodie 3 with Bibilab’s Neko House Desk and Cat tower Rack The Meowgaroo Hoodie 3 is available in medium and large sizes, and can be ordered for 8,900 yen (US$56) through Amazon Japan here . title: Kenshi Yonezu’s Lemon hits 1 billion views on YouTube and he’s still not quite sure why
summary: He handed life a ‘Lemon.’ Back in 2018, one song in particular was tearing up the charts in Japan. It was a somewhat somber pop song balanced with an energetic rock rhythm, known as ‘Lemon.’ It won several awards, was played on calculators, and in addition to charting number one on the Billboard Japan Hot […]
details: He handed life a ‘Lemon.’ Back in 2018, one song in particular was tearing up the charts in Japan. It was a somewhat somber pop song balanced with an energetic rock rhythm, known as ‘ Lemon .’ It won several awards, was played on calculators , and in addition to charting number one on the Billboard Japan Hot 100 for 2018, it has continued to chart in the annual Hot 100 every year since. Now, eight years since its initial release, the song has earned yet another honor by surpassing one billion views on YouTube . It’s rarefied air that ‘Lemon’ now shares with the likes of ‘Baby Shark,’ and in honor of this achievement, songwriter Kenshi Yonezu released the following statement, translated from Japanese : “In all honesty, I still don’t really get why ‘Lemon’ became such a huge song with this wide a reach. I mean, of course I never set out to make a trivial piece of music, and I totally get that Lemon only grew into a phenomenon because it was the theme song for the truly excellent television show Unnatural , and because the production team treated it with the utmost care and affection. But I remember back when I first released Lemon, I was completely blown away by the explosive momentum its reputation spread with. I thought to myself, ‘Hang on… Is this really going to be my signature song?’ It was like lighting a small scrap of wood on fire, thinking I’d start a campfire, only to have the flames spread instantly and eventually turn into a full-blown wildfire with me just standing there holding a lighter in one hand and a bucket of water in the other. That’s how the whole situation looked from my perspective. When I was growing up, I’d see these brilliant musicians act dismissive about their own signature songs, claiming they never saw what was so good about them or refusing to play them live because they didn’t like them. At the time, I’d think to myself, ‘It’s clearly a great song! Don’t play cool and act like you don’t know it!’ But now that it’s happened to me, I finally understand why they felt the way they did. To put it simply, songs like this end up leaving the creator’s original intentions and personal feelings in the dust. They move at such an incredible speed they basically become public domain overnight. I guess it’s only natural to resent that a little bit. In a way, ‘Lemon’ has allowed me to pull up a chair at the same table as these great musicians, at least in the sense that I can empathize with them now. It might sound like I’m complaining, but I want to be clear that I have always felt and always will feel tremendous gratitude towards ‘Lemon.’ It took an untamed, raggedy stray dog from the sticks like me and threw my life into complete chaos. It showed me sights that I’d never dream of seeing and guided me into a life so absurdly entertaining that it nearly wears me out. Some nights I imagine myself in the future as a pathetic and withered old man singing ‘Lemon’ and strumming along in front of some kids 40 years younger than me. They’d bluntly tell me off, saying, ‘Give all those depressing songs a break,’ and ‘No one even remembers that song anymore,’ but that’s just the way it is.” It’s good to see the fame hasn’t changed Yonezu much. He still seems to be the somewhat brooding but incredibly insightful guy he was eight years ago. Online comments were also intrigued by his surprisingly astute and sincere reflections on having a billion-view song. “What a wonderful statement that really conveys Yonezu’s true feelings and sense of astonishment about this.” “Wow! Last time I checked, it was about 600 million.” “He’s totally talking about Bump of Chicken and ‘Tentai Kansoku’ in that middle part, lol!” “He’s really got class. You can see how he struggles to process how the public reaction doesn’t align with his own assessment of his work without sounding bitter about it.” “He’s an artist, musician, and a great writer too.” “That comment makes me happy! Congratulations on ‘Lemon’ hitting a billion views!” “It’s the classic story. The things an artist doesn’t try too hard to make end up being the most highly regarded.” “What an annoyingly long-winded rant. I read the whole thing, but still…” “He should try writing an autobiography sometime. I’d like to read it.” “I like the way he writes about ‘Lemon’ better than ‘Lemon.’” I kind of agree that ‘Lemon’ isn’t even really Yonezu firing on all cylinders, and would argue he’s done some stuff much more deserving of a billion views. However, the part about him feeling bad when people misunderstand his work is really making me nervous about our 1,000-word analysis of how ‘Paprika’ is really about children who died . He’s never copped to it, but I’d eat my hat if it isn’t. Source: Reissue Records , My Game News Flash Image: Pakutaso ● Want to hear about SoraNews24’s latest articles as soon as they’re published? title: New Era celebrates three decades of Pokémon with new 30th anniversary cap line [Photos]
summary: Every Pokémon Trainer needs a hat, right? Over his multiple decades as the protagonist of the Pokémon anime, Satoshi/Ash taught fans many things. The importance of believing in yourself. The power of friendship. And, of course, that no matter where your journeys in life may take you, a good hat is always nice to have. […]
details: Every Pokémon Trainer needs a hat, right? Over his multiple decades as the protagonist of the Pokémon anime, Satoshi/Ash taught fans many things. The importance of believing in yourself. The power of friendship. And, of course, that no matter where your journeys in life may take you, a good hat is always nice to have. The first two of those are things that you can only achieve through personal courage and life experience, but the third is something that New Era is ready to provide, through its new Pokémon collaboration line . Part of the ongoing celebration of the Pokémon franchise’s 30th anniversary, New Era has crafted a collection featuring an all-star cast of creatures. One of the most eye-catching, from any angle, is the 59 Fifty Pokémon 30 All Over cap, with Pikachu on the front and Venusaur, Charizard, and Blastoise covering the other sides . The original starter trio show up in their pre-evolution forms too, with Bulbasaur, Charmander, and Squirtle, plus Pikachu too, printed all across the cap’s lining . If that’s too busy for your tastes, this 59 Fifty has them hanging out together on the front, with the 30th anniversary emblem on the right side and the Pokémon logo on the back. Meanwhile, Mew’s intimidating presence means that he has the front of his 59 Fifty all to himself. Moving on to more abstract expressions of Pokémon, the Pikachu 9 Forty A-frame Trucker caps render the series mascot in rhinestones , with your choice of three different color schemes. And for those looking for a more understated style, New Era has a whole slew of 9 Twenty caps for fans of Pikachu, Eevee, Ditto, Mewtwo, and the Gen-1 starters . ▼ Mewtwo’s heart-shaped tail pose is an especially charming touch. Prices range from 4,950 yen (US$31) for the 9 Twenty caps to 5,500 for the 9 Forty and 7,700 for the 59 Fifty models. The lineup goes on sale November 20 at New Era stores in Japan and through the New Era online shop here .
