title: Two Tokyo neighborhoods to gather on bridge and shift their recognized border through tug-of-war
summary: Sibling ward rivalry doesn’t need solid ground for its bragging-rights battlefield. My parents were very strict about the Baseel brothers not fighting with each other while we were growing up, but I’ve been told that it’s not unusual for siblings to squabble. And so it is that Tokyo’s Sumida and Taito Wards, neighbors who have […]
details: Sibling ward rivalry doesn’t need solid ground for its bragging-rights battlefield . My parents were very strict about the Baseel brothers not fighting with each other while we were growing up, but I’ve been told that it’s not unusual for siblings to squabble. And so it is that Tokyo’s Sumida and Taito Wards , neighbors who have been sister wards since 1977, have begun meeting every year and attempting to expand their territory at the other’s expense by shifting the symbolic borderline between the two . Fittingly, the two parties want this annual contest to take place on their border, but that presents a bit of a problem, since flowing between Sumida and Taito is the Sumida River . They’ve managed to work out a solution, though, and so later this month the Sakurabashi Bridge will once again become the scene of the Sumida River Tug-of-War Tournament . The exact mid-point of the bridge is one of the very few publicly accessible points along the wards’ borderline, and the only one exclusively for pedestrian crossings. S o since 2024, Sumida and Taito have been sending teams of representatives for a series of tug-of-war battles to be waged on Sakurabashi, with the agreement that both wards will recognize that the border has been moved by one meter (3.3 feet) in the direction of the losing ward, giving the winner that much larger of a domain . ▼ Video of the 2025 Sumida River Tug-of-War Tournament For the last two years, Taito has won the tournament, as documented in this illustration showing the border in 2023 (yellow line), 2024 (dotted red line), and 2025 (solid red line) ▼ The Sakurabashi Bridge, with the Tokyo Skytree standing tall on the Sumida Ward side of the river It should be noted that while Tokyo’s wards do each have some level of autonomy, the municipal-level administration doesn’t actually let its component parts go around redrawing their boundaries, and so the territorial prize at stake in the Sumida River Tug-of-War Tournament is really a symbolic one (this is also why the tournament is followed by a friendly celebration at a riverside terrace). The length of the bridge also means that neither ward is likely to reach the opposite riverbank, barring some sort of highly localized protein deficiency that leaves one group of residents significantly weaker than the other for several decades. Nevertheless, there’s civic pride at stake, and Sumida is no doubt eager to avenge its two consecutive losses. Rather than recruiting entire teams, participants apply to their ward individually, with organizers assembling 12 teams, including two children’s teams, of 10 members each from the pool. On the day of the tournament, opposing teams will compete in a best-two-out-of-three format, and in order to prevent a 6-6 tie, each ward also puts together an all-star team , made up of members of its 12 others, for a 13th match. This year’s Sumida River Tug-of-War Tournament is scheduled to start at 10:30 a.m. on November 15 atop the Sakurabashi Bridge, which is roughly a 15-minute walk from Asakusa Station in Taito Ward or Oshiage Station in Sumida Ward . It’ll also be the first year for the broadcasting club of Taito’s Iwakura High School to be on-site providing live color commentary , which should give the whole event some good “crazy anime series sports episode” energy. ▼ Sakurabashi Bridge As of this writing, Sumida Ward is still accepting applicants through the event’s official website, but even if you’re not pulling, spectators are welcome to come out and cheer one, or both, of the sides on, with no admission tickets required . title: Dragon Ball Daima borra a Mr. Popo en Francia, ¡pero su voz sigue apareciendo!
summary: Dragon Ball Daima desata polémica en Francia por eliminar a Mr. Popo de las escenas, aunque su voz sigue presente. Alemania aplicó cambios similares.
details: Anime Dragon Ball Daima borra a Mr. Popo en Francia, ¡pero su voz sigue apareciendo! La televisión francesa eliminó al personaje de las imágenes, aunque todavía se escuchan sus diálogos. Mirukaru hace 2 horas 1 Comentarios ADS Imagínate estar viendo Dragon Ball Daima y escuchar a uno de los personajes hablando con toda normalidad, pero sin que aparezca por ninguna parte. Pues eso es exactamente lo que ocurrió en Francia, donde Mr. Popo fue eliminado visualmente de la versión televisiva del anime . El personaje desapareció de varias escenas mediante recortes y modificaciones de imagen, aunque sus diálogos todavía pueden escucharse. Y lo más curioso es que no se trata de la primera vez que ocurre algo parecido en Europa. La controversia comenzó el pasado 4 de noviembre de 2026 , cuando Dragon Ball Daima debutó en la televisión francesa a través del canal Gulli. Los espectadores que ya conocían la versión original notaron rápidamente que Mr. Popo, el histórico ayudante de Kami-sama y posteriormente de Dende, había desaparecido de las escenas donde normalmente debería encontrarse. Pero no se limitaron a quitar una o dos apariciones. Según las comparaciones compartidas por los seguidores, algunas secuencias fueron eliminadas por completo, mientras que otras recibieron acercamientos y cambios de encuadre para dejar al personaje fuera de la pantalla. En determinados momentos incluso se modificaron escenas retrospectivas donde aparecía junto a otros personajes. El resultado es bastante extraño, especialmente para quienes nunca han visto la serie. En algunas conversaciones, Mr. Popo sigue participando mediante sus diálogos, pero nadie puede verlo. Es decir, el personaje continúa existiendo dentro de la historia, aunque la edición televisiva parece empeñada en que los espectadores no lo conozcan. Mr. Popo ya había desaparecido de Dragon Ball Daima en Alemania Lo más sorprendente es que la televisión alemana aplicó modificaciones prácticamente idénticas cuando Dragon Ball Daima comenzó a transmitirse por Toggo Plus el pasado 28 de agosto. En aquella ocasión, los espectadores también detectaron escenas recortadas, acercamientos de cámara y diálogos donde Mr. Popo seguía hablando sin aparecer en pantalla. Por ahora, ni Gulli ni Toei Animation Europe han explicado públicamente quién ordenó estos cambios o cuáles fueron sus motivos . Sin embargo, diversos medios franceses han señalado que la apariencia de Mr. Popo lleva décadas generando controversia debido a las similitudes que algunos críticos encuentran entre su diseño y antiguas caricaturas racistas de personas negras. De hecho, no sería la primera vez que su apariencia termina modificada para una emisión occidental. En una versión estadounidense de Dragon Ball Z Kai , transmitida en 2010, la piel de Mr. Popo fue cambiada a color azul . Aquella decisión también provocó numerosas discusiones entre los seguidores de la franquicia. Eso sí, conviene aclarar que las modificaciones actuales corresponden a versiones destinadas a la televisión europea. Los 20 episodios de Dragon Ball Daima continúan disponibles sin estos recortes en plataformas como Crunchyroll y Netflix en Francia, donde los espectadores pueden ver al personaje tal como aparece en la versión japonesa. La situación resulta particularmente llamativa porque Dragon Ball Daima incluye detalles sobre los orígenes de Mr. Popo y su relación con el Reino de los Demonios. Al eliminar sus apariciones, los espectadores de estas emisiones televisivas también pierden parte de la información que la propia historia presenta sobre él. ¿Crees que cambiar el color de Mr. Popo habría sido una solución menos extraña, o consideras que deberían transmitir Dragon Ball Daima tal como fue creado, sin convertir al personaje en una voz invisible? title: 33-sai Dokushin Onna Kishi Taichou tendrá anime: 33 años, soltera y explotada
summary: El manga para adultos 33-sai Dokushin Onna Kishi Taichou, del creador de Ishuzoku Reviewers, tendrá anime y presentó sus primeros diseños y un video musical.
details: Anime 33-sai Dokushin Onna Kishi Taichou tendrá anime: 33 años, soltera y explotada El creador de Ishuzoku Reviewers regresa con una comedia para adultos sobre una caballera sin tiempo para el amor. Kenji hace 5 horas 0 Comentarios ADS Ser una heroína de fantasía suena bastante emocionante, hasta que descubres que también puedes terminar explotada en el trabajo y sin tiempo para conseguir pareja. Esa es precisamente la situación de Mail, la protagonista de 33-sai Dokushin Onna Kishi Taichou , el manga de Amahara que recibirá una adaptación al anime . El anuncio fue realizado por Digital Shokunin para celebrar el décimo aniversario de la obra, acompañado de los primeros diseños de personajes y un video musical. Y si el nombre de Amahara te resulta familiar, probablemente sea porque también es el creador de Ishuzoku Reviewers , aquella comedia de fantasía para adultos que dio bastante de qué hablar cuando recibió su adaptación animada en 2020. Así que, como podrás imaginar, su nueva obra tampoco será precisamente una historia sobre caballeros que se limitan a rescatar princesas. Una caballera de 33 años que no tiene tiempo ni para conseguir novio La historia sigue a Mail, una capitana de caballería de 33 años que continúa soltera y cuya vida está dominada por unas condiciones laborales bastante miserables. Entre las responsabilidades de su puesto y las interminables jornadas de trabajo, apenas encuentra oportunidades para conocer a alguien o disfrutar de su vida personal. De hecho, sus escasos días libres suelen terminar entre bebidas alcohólicas, descanso y maneras de satisfacer sus necesidades íntimas. Y no es la única que atraviesa semejante situación, pues sus compañeras también deben lidiar con el agotamiento, los problemas del trabajo y sus propios deseos sexuales. Todo ello da forma a una comedia de fantasía para adultos que se burla tanto de los clichés de los caballeros como de la vida laboral moderna. Para celebrar el anuncio, la producción compartió un video musical con la canción Boogieing Dance Kishi , interpretada por Sekka y compuesta por Suzumi. El material utiliza ilustraciones de la obra y sirve como presentación del proyecto, aunque todavía no se trata de un tráiler convencional con escenas del anime. También se dieron a conocer el logotipo oficial y los primeros diseños de los personajes. Amahara bromeó con tener un anime y terminó haciéndose realidad Pero quizá lo más curioso de este anuncio sea la manera en que el propio autor se enteró de la adaptación. Amahara explicó que, mientras preparaba el epílogo del cuarto volumen del manga, dibujó una broma preguntándose si la obra conseguiría un anime para celebrar su décimo aniversario. Aproximadamente una semana después de entregar aquel material, le comunicaron que el proyecto había sido aprobado . Parece que hasta sus bromas terminan convirtiéndose en realidad. El manga comenzó su publicación en octubre de 2015 dentro de la revista digital para adultos Ananga Ranga , de KATTS, y continúa publicándose de manera irregular. Su cuarto volumen recopilatorio llegó a las tiendas japonesas el 15 de enero de 2026 bajo el sello de Flex Comics. Por ahora, no se ha revelado una fecha de estreno, estudio de animación ni elenco de voces . Tampoco se ha especificado qué formato tendrá la adaptación, así que habrá que esperar nuevos anuncios para saber cómo trasladarán a la pantalla el humor subido de tono de la obra original. ¿Te llama la atención una fantasía donde el mayor enemigo de una caballera no es un dragón, sino trabajar demasiado y seguir soltera a los 33 años? title: Killing Bites llega a su final después de casi 13 años de combates salvajes
summary: Killing Bites terminó después de casi 13 años de publicación. El manga concluyó con su capítulo 145 y lanzará su volumen final en diciembre de 2026.
details: Manga Killing Bites llega a su final después de casi 13 años de combates salvajes El manga terminó con su capítulo 145 y publicará su volumen 28 y definitivo el próximo 25 de diciembre. Yuna hace 2 horas 2 Comentarios ADS Después de tantos años viendo a humanos con habilidades animales despedazarse en combates donde prácticamente todo estaba permitido, finalmente llegó el momento de conocer el desenlace. El manga Killing Bites concluyó oficialmente su publicación el pasado 23 de octubre con el lanzamiento de su capítulo 145, poniendo fin a una historia que acompañó a sus lectores durante casi 13 años. La obra, escrita por Shinya Murata e ilustrada por Kazasa Sumita , comenzó a publicarse en noviembre de 2013 dentro de la revista Monthly Hero's . Sin embargo, después del cierre de dicha publicación en 2020, la serie encontró un nuevo hogar en la plataforma digital Comiplex, donde continuó desarrollando sus enfrentamientos hasta alcanzar su conclusión. Y aunque la historia ya terminó, los coleccionistas todavía tienen una última cita pendiente. Se confirmó que el volumen 28 y definitivo saldrá a la venta el 25 de diciembre de 2026 en Japón, reuniendo los capítulos restantes y marcando el cierre editorial de la franquicia. Para celebrar el final, ambos autores compartieron mensajes de agradecimiento. Murata recordó la pregunta que acompañó a la obra desde sus inicios: ¿cuál es la bestia más fuerte? Un viaje a 1907 que comienza con un compromiso inesperado La historia sigue a Hina Katagiri, una estudiante de preparatoria que tiene un sueño recurrente cada vez que llueve. En él aparece su versión infantil jugando con un niño en un jardín que no reconoce. Sin embargo, un día termina encontrando ese mismo lugar en la realidad y, antes de comprender qué está sucediendo, aparece en el Japón de 1907. Allí conoce a Takaaki Hongo , un joven heredero de una familia adinerada que, para sorpresa de Hina, la confunde con su prometida, Hinako. El muchacho está tan convencido de haberla encontrado que decide acompañarla hasta su supuesto hogar, pero la situación se complica cuando la protagonista descubre que existe otra chica prácticamente idéntica a ella . Ahora Hina tendrá que descubrir por qué terminó viajando al pasado, qué relación existe entre sus sueños y aquel misterioso joven, y cómo regresar a su propia época. Este último también realizó la primera imagen promocional, que apuesta por una estética delicada y una ambientación acorde con la época en la que transcurre buena parte de la historia. Cabe recordar que Rainy Day Serenade , conocido en Japón como Namidaame to Serenade , comenzó su publicación en noviembre de 2014 dentro de la revista Kiss de Kodansha. Todo cambia cuando Hana despierta repentinamente un poder extraordinario. Pero, en lugar de aprovechar la oportunidad para demostrar que todos estaban equivocados, decide ocultar sus habilidades y continuar viviendo tranquilamente . El muchacho está buscando una esposa capaz de acompañarlo en sus responsabilidades y, después de conocer el verdadero potencial de Hana, le propone un matrimonio por contrato . Rina Sato regresará como Haruka Minami, Marina Inoue interpretará nuevamente a Kana Minami y Minori Chihara volverá como Chiaki Minami. Y no serán las únicas. También está confirmado el regreso de Nana Mizuki como Toma Minami, Rika Morinaga como Makoto, Tetsuya Kakihara como Fujioka y Daisuke Ono como Hosaka, entre otros integrantes del elenco que participaron en las temporadas anteriores. En cuanto al equipo de producción, Junichi Kitamura dirigirá la serie en LIDENFILMS , estudio conocido por trabajos como Tokyo Revengers . Takamitsu Kono estará a cargo de la composición de la serie, mientras que Nobuhiro Ando se encargará del diseño de personajes. Por otra parte, Yasuhiro Misawa regresará para componer la música, acompañado de Yasunori Ebina en la dirección de sonido. Para quienes no estén familiarizados con la franquicia, Minami-ke sigue la vida cotidiana de tres hermanas con personalidades completamente diferentes. Haruka es la mayor y prácticamente se encarga de mantener el orden en casa, Kana es una especialista en causar problemas y Chiaki, la menor, nunca pierde una oportunidad para burlarse de su hermana del medio. Lo curioso es que la serie no necesita grandes acontecimientos para funcionar. Entre las tareas escolares, las visitas de sus amigos y las discusiones más absurdas, las tres consiguen convertir cualquier situación cotidiana en una comedia. De hecho, los responsables recuperaron una advertencia que acompaña a la franquicia desde hace años: esta es simplemente una historia sobre la vida diaria de las hermanas Minami, así que no esperen demasiado . Una espera que comenzó en 2013 Cabe recordar que el anime de Minami-ke comenzó sus emisiones en octubre de 2007, seguido por Minami-ke: Okawari en 2008, Minami-ke: Okaeri en 2009 y Minami-ke: Tadaima en 2013. Desde entonces, la franquicia no había recibido otra temporada televisiva, aunque su manga original continuó publicándose. La obra de Koharu Sakuraba comenzó su serialización en 2004 dentro de la revista Weekly Young Magazine de Kodansha y actualmente cuenta con 29 volúmenes recopilatorios y más de cinco millones de copias en circulación . La producción de una nueva temporada había sido anunciada en 2024, durante las celebraciones por el vigésimo aniversario del manga, pero hasta ahora no se había confirmado su fecha de estreno. Por el momento, abril de 2027 es la única fecha anunciada , sin detalles sobre el día exacto ni las plataformas que transmitirán la serie internacionalmente. Al menos ahora los seguidores saben que podrán volver a visitar a las hermanas Minami después de una espera que parecía interminable. ¿Todavía recuerdas las peleas entre Kana y Chiaki, o han pasado tantos años que necesitarás volver a ver las cuatro temporadas anteriores para prepararte para su regreso? title: Bless tiene fecha: él sueña con maquillar y ella con convertirse en modelo
summary: Bless revela su primer tráiler y confirma su estreno el 8 de enero de 2027. A-1 Pictures animará esta historia de moda, maquillaje y superación personal.
details: Anime Bless tiene fecha: él sueña con maquillar y ella con convertirse en modelo Dos estudiantes desafiarán los estándares de belleza en este anime de A-1 Pictures que llegará en enero de 2027. Mirukaru hace 1 hora 0 Comentarios ADS Que todos te digan que tienes cara de modelo debe ser fantástico, a menos que tu verdadero sueño sea dedicarte al maquillaje. Esa es la situación de uno de los protagonistas de Bless , el manga de Yukino Sonoyama que pronto llegará a la televisión. La producción presentó su primer tráiler completo y una nueva imagen promocional , confirmando que el anime se estrenará el 8 de enero de 2027 bajo la animación de A-1 Pictures. El avance nos presenta a Aia Udagawa y Jun Sumisaki, dos estudiantes que tienen algo en común: ninguno se atreve a perseguir lo que realmente quiere. También permite escuchar un fragmento de New Page , el ending interpretado por HIKKA , cuya letra está inspirada en las dificultades de encontrar la propia identidad y reunir el valor para seguir adelante. Por otra parte, la imagen promocional muestra a los protagonistas dentro de una composición que recuerda a una paleta de sombras para ojos, rodeados de diferentes productos de maquillaje. Una elección bastante apropiada para una historia donde los cosméticos no sirven simplemente para cambiar la apariencia de alguien, sino también para ayudarlo a descubrir una nueva faceta de sí mismo. Bless contará una historia sobre maquillaje, moda y sueños frustrados La historia sigue a Aia Udagawa , un muchacho que desde pequeño ha recibido comentarios sobre su apariencia y su supuesto futuro como modelo. Sin embargo, lo que realmente desea es convertirse en maquillista profesional, un sueño que terminó ocultando por miedo a las opiniones de quienes lo rodean. Por otro lado tenemos a Jun Sumisaki , una estudiante alta y con pecas que ha sufrido burlas por su apariencia. Aunque le gustaría dedicarse al modelaje, sus inseguridades le impiden imaginarse frente a una cámara o desfilando por una pasarela. Curiosamente, los dos parecen tener exactamente lo que el otro necesita para comenzar a cambiar su vida. Todo comienza cuando ambos son seleccionados para participar en un concurso de moda durante el festival escolar. Inicialmente, Aia debía encargarse del modelaje y Jun del vestuario, pero terminan intercambiando sus funciones. Así, él tendrá la oportunidad de demostrar su talento con el maquillaje y ella podrá experimentar lo que significa convertirse en modelo . Eso sí, entrar al mundo de la moda no será tan sencillo como descubrir una habilidad oculta. Los protagonistas deberán enfrentarse a sus propias inseguridades, las expectativas de los demás y la competencia de una industria donde la apariencia suele ser juzgada constantemente. En cuanto al elenco de voces, Tomohiro Ono interpretará a Aia Udagawa , mientras que Chiyuki Miura dará voz a Jun Sumisaki . La dirección estará a cargo de Shotaro Kitamura en el estudio A-1 Pictures, con Fukuro Kamiza como responsable de los guiones y Honoka Yokoyama en el diseño de personajes. El anime comenzará sus emisiones el 8 de enero a las 23:30 horas en el bloque Noitamina de Fuji TV . Además, Crunchyroll confirmó que transmitirá la serie internacionalmente , incluyendo Latinoamérica, como parte de su catálogo de invierno de 2027. Cabe recordar que el manga original de Bless comenzó a publicarse en enero de 2022 y actualmente continúa su serialización en la revista Monthly Shonen Sirius de Kodansha. La obra ya supera 1.25 millones de copias en circulación , una cifra que demuestra el interés que ha despertado esta historia sobre belleza, esfuerzo y aceptación personal. ¿Te llaman la atención los animes que exploran el mundo de la moda y el maquillaje, o lo que más te interesa de Bless es ver cómo Aia y Jun aprenden a dejar de vivir según las expectativas de los demás? title: Hello Kitty ready to keep you company in the bathroom with new dessert-aroma Sanrio toilet paper
summary: It’s like a skating party in your bathroom, and all your Sanrio friends are invited. Part of the secret to the enduring popularity of Hello Kitty and her Sanrio pals is what loyal friends they are. Sure, you could take the cynical interpretation that their incredibly wide variety of character merch is simply a way […]
details: It’s like a skating party in your bathroom, and all your Sanrio friends are invited . Part of the secret to the enduring popularity of Hello Kitty and her Sanrio pals is what loyal friends they are. Sure, you could take the cynical interpretation that their incredibly wide variety of character merch is simply a way to multiply revenue streams, but there’s no denying that it also means that almost no matter what you’re doing in life, there’s a way for you to do it with your favorite Sanrio characters keeping you company…even in the bathroom. This week, Fukuoka-based paper products company Marutomi Seishi began selling its newest collaboration with Sanrio, the “Sanrio Winter 12-Roll Double.” And yes, that’s “double” as in “double-ply toilet paper.” This isn’t just a case of playful packaging, either, the paper itself is covered in illustrations . ▼ It’s only fitting that Sanrio toilet paper be as kind and gentle as the characters that appear on it. Over a dozen Sanrio characters are featured, including Helloy Kitty, Pompompurin, Cinnamoroll, My Melody, Kuromi, Pochacco, and Hangyodon , on two patterns. The new paper has a wintery motif, depicting the Sanrio friends bundled up for an ice skating outing rendered in a cool snowy color scheme. Marutomi Seishi also promises that the Sanrio toiler paper has a “sweets fragrance.” That’s not to be confused with a generic “sweet” smell, but instead appears to indicate that this toilet paper has the aroma of some sort of dessert. The goal, Marutomi Seishi says, is for the Sanrio toilet paper to “create a peaceful, tranquil atmosphere in your bathroom,” and the 12-roll pack should be showing up now in Japanese drugstores and other housewares retailers. title: Cinnabon gets into the Japanese spirit with new Wagokorobon treats
summary: Cinnabon Japan finds two new ways to mix its own dessert traditions with Japan’s. Unlike some other American sweets suppliers who’ve set up shop in Japan, Cinnabon doesn’t have Japan-exclusive menu items all that often. We can probably chalk that up to the chain’s key ingredient, cinnamon, being a distinct flavor that doesn’t feature very […]
details: Cinnabon Japan finds two new ways to mix its own dessert traditions with Japan’s . Unlike some other American sweets suppliers who’ve set up shop in Japan, Cinnabon doesn’t have Japan-exclusive menu items all that often. We can probably chalk that up to the chain’s key ingredient, cinnamon, being a distinct flavor that doesn’t feature very often at all in traditional Japanese desserts. Leave the cinnamon in, and it’s hard to find a cordial combo with Japanese ingredients, but take it out, and it’s not really a cinnamon bun anymore, is it? But every now and again Cinnabon Japan does find a way to create new desserts with Japanese inspirations, and it’s got two on its menu right now. Collectively called the Wagokorobon line ( wagokoro meaning “Japanese heart”), the first of the two items is the Kuri (Chestnut) Matcha Mini Chocobon . This starts as one of Cinnabon’s cinnamon-light Chocobons, which get chocolate kneaded into the standard Cinnabon dough plus a drizzle of chocolate sauce. This Wagokorobon version also gets a chestnut frosting , representing one of Japan’s favorite fall dessert flavors, plus a whole lot of matcha sprinkled on top . There’s so much green tea that it looks like it’ll definitely impart a noticeable texture, but that powdery sensation shouldn’t be too far off from the sprinkled cinnamon on conventional cinnamon buns. Meanwhile, there’s a different granular guest star on the Kuromitsu Kinako Minibon : kinako , or roasted soybean powder. While not as sweet as the sweet red bean paste called anko that often shows up in Japanese confectioneries, kinako is noticeably sweet and fragrant, with a slight nutty quality to its flavor. Kinako’s texture is fine enough that it can make the things it’s sprinkled on feel a little dry, though, so it’s often accompanied by kuromitsu , a kind of Japanese brown sugar molasses, as it is here, and the mix of sweet, sticky, powdery sensations should slot very nicely into what you’d want from a cinnamon bun while still having an unmistakably Japanese taste. Both Wagokorobon items are on sale at Cinnabon Japan branches now, and are scheduled to be available until late November. title: Japan’s new matcha vending machines serve freshly prepared matcha in five different strengths
summary: Enjoy the taste of freshly whisked matcha at the touch of a button. Japan is home to many different types of vending machines, and some of the most impressive are the ones that serve freshly ground coffee, with the beans ground and each cup brewed to order inside the machine. The process is even shown […]
details: Enjoy the taste of freshly whisked matcha at the touch of a button. Japan is home to many different types of vending machines, and some of the most impressive are the ones that serve freshly ground coffee, with the beans ground and each cup brewed to order inside the machine . The process is even shown live on a monitor, so customers can watch their coffee being prepared. Now, Toyo Vending , the company behind the popular Mill-Ground Coffee vending machines, has teamed up with tea giant Ito En to bring this technology to powdered green tea . The result is “ Japan Quality Matcha ”, a new style of drink that uses carefully selected matcha ingredients and specialised preparation technology to deliver an authentic taste similar to freshly whisked matcha, with five different strengths to choose from. The new machines aim to cater to the growing demand for matcha , making it even more accessible and convenient, particularly for overseas visitors. Unlike regular drink vending machines, which are filled with bottles and cans, these ones prepare drinks to order, with the process beginning only after the customer presses the button . The company says its technology produces a taste similar to freshly whisked matcha , while also allowing customers to choose how strong they want their drink. The machines are easy to spot, with three different all-green designs, each of which takes its inspiration from Japanese scenery and traditional culture. The first design features a deep green colour inspired by Japanese landscapes, designed to evoke a sense of tranquillity and relaxation. The second features traditional Japanese patterns, while the third, described as “Modern Luxury”, combines a large display screen with an image of matcha against a premium tea plantation. The machines are set to be located at high-traffic locations like expressway rest areas, train stations, airports, commercial facilities, and tourist destinations popular with international visitors. These machines are an exciting new way to enjoy matcha, and are already beginning to generate a lot of buzz in Japan. Their uniqueness has been summed up by Toyo Vending CEO Yoshimasa Wakamatsu, who has this message for matcha fans. “We have always been committed to providing an uncompromising cup of coffee through our Mill-Ground Coffee machines, and now we’ve applied that same technology to matcha, one of Japan’s traditional treasures. We’re delighted to have found such an excellent partner in Ito En and to be able to deliver authentic Japan Quality to customers both in Japan and overseas. Through the familiarity of vending machines, we hope to offer a new way to experience matcha.” We certainly can’t wait to try the new matcha, and all five different strengths that allow you to select your preferred intensity, when they begin appearing around Japan this month. With a variety of options to choose from, including regular matcha and matcha lattes, these look set to become the next hot trend to flood your socials, so keep an eye out for them during your travels. title: Restaurant opens in Japan with all-dementia waitresses, serves up ramen, awareness, and kindness
summary: Restaurant of Mistaken Orders is upfront about potential problems in order to cultivate future understanding. Japan has incredibly high customer service standards, especially where restaurants are concerned. Because of that, a restaurant saying, in advance, that it might get your order wrong seems like a recipe for dissatisfied diners, but that strategy led to smiles […]
details: Restaurant of Mistaken Orders is upfront about potential problems in order to cultivate future understanding . Japan has incredibly high customer service standards, especially where restaurants are concerned. Because of that, a restaurant saying, in advance, that it might get your order wrong seems like a recipe for dissatisfied diners, but that strategy led to smiles all around, plus a few appreciative tears, recently in the city of Matsuyama, Ehime Prefecture . “Restaurant of Mistaken Orders” didn’t get its unusual name through a translation error, as that really is a pretty accurate rendering of its Japanese name, Chumon wo Machigaeru Kamoshirenai Ryori-ten. That less-than-perfect precision isn’t due to a lack of effort or concern on the restaurant’s part, though, but because the waitstaff is composed of senior citizens with dementia . Restaurant of Mistaken Orders, which started out in 2018, operates on a popup basis, partnering with preexisting restaurants which serve as a venue for the unique eatery for the day. For its most recent iteration in Matsuyama, Restaurant of Mistaken Orders teamed up with Tenryu Ramen on September 21, which was both the Japanese public holiday Respect for the Aged Day and World Alzheimer’s Day. ▼ Restaurant of Mistaken Orders at Tenryu Ramen It should be pointed out that the driving philosophy behind Restaurant of Mistaken Orders is not “Let’s get those dementia-stricken seniors working!” Instead, the purpose of the venture is to foster a greater sense of awareness and consideration towards people living with dementia, and also to give the participating seniors a sense of confidence and accomplishment by showing that their condition doesn’t have to mean complete debilitation and isolation from human interaction . “We hope this feeling of openness and understanding will spread across Japan, and through the world” says the organization in is mission statement, showing that the restaurant setting is meant to serve as a sort of metaphor for kindness wherever one may encounter someone with dementia. In Matsuyama, four local seniors, ranging in age from 78 to 88, took orders and served diners , including the daughter and granddaughter of one of the participants (the daughter is the woman who can be seen wiping away tears in the above video, while talking about how emotionally moving it is to see her mother staying active). “If we took our time and listened and spoke patiently, we could understand each other,” says a father of a family of four that are at Restaurant of Mistaken Orders of communicating with the staff, and one of the elderly waitresses, at the end of the event, said with a smile “I was really happy to get to see so many people and talk with them.” ▼ The project’s concept video With community outreach and public awareness being the primary goals, operating profits aren’t really a priority for Restaurant of Mistaken Orders, and the organization accepts online donations here for those that aren’t able to come in for a bite to eat, but still want to lend a helping hand. title: Get the taste of the U.K. in Tokyo with 99 Flakes, meat pies, and Jaffa Cakes
summary: This tiny Shibuya spot brings quintessential UK snacks straight to central Tokyo. Whether you have moved to a different country and pining for the foodstuffs of the motherland or you are interested in foreign cuisine without the hefty price tag of the airfare, specialty import stores are a treat to walk around. Tucked away amid […]
details: This tiny Shibuya spot brings quintessential UK snacks straight to central Tokyo. Whether you have moved to a different country and pining for the foodstuffs of the motherland or you are interested in foreign cuisine without the hefty price tag of the airfare, specialty import stores are a treat to walk around. Tucked away amid the towering buildings of Shibuya , you’ll find The British Shop , a grocery store specializing in British ingredients with its own eat-in area. Located just outside exit B3 of the Shibuya subway station , The British Shop’s footprint is even smaller than a convenience store, but the shelves are lined with British foods and a table is set up in the center from which you can enjoy a variety of foods. One of the highlights for a nostalgic Brit would be the ice cream van staple of a 99 Flake , essentially a soft-serve ice cream cone with a Cadbury’s Flake chocolate bar inserted into it. Unfortunately, sales were suspended on the day we visited, but we still got to enjoy some chocolatey goodness with our ice cream. To satisfy our ice cream cravings, we opted for a double scoop (750 yen [US$4.74]) along with a Flake (100 yen): the first scoop was vanilla and clotted cream , and the second blackcurrant and double cream . While clotted cream is an indispensable accompaniment to scones, it has to be said that seeing it as an ice cream flavor is pretty unusual. The taste was unexpectedly light with a gentle sweetness, reproducing the lightness of actual clotted cream. Combining a subtly milky taste with the rich aroma of vanilla made for an addictive, delicious flavor. Blackcurrant is known as ‘cassis’ in Japan, where it is arguably seen most as a part of alcoholic drinks, but in the UK it is much more widely enjoyed in squashes (fruit cordials) or as a component to desserts. The tartness of the ice cream wasn’t too strong, and had a taste that made us keep coming back in for another scoop. After spending any amount of time in Japan, you come to realize that ‘pies’ are almost always of the dessert variety, often containing fruits, but at this little shop you can purchase the Chunky Beef Pie for 600 yen, which is made with huge chunks of diced beef and has a very rich taste. After coming all the way to the store, it would be unthinkable if you left without picking up some snacks as a souvenir, and what better way to do that than to take home the subject of Britain’s biggest snack debate: the Jaffa Cake (520 yen). Delectable treats made by layering a soft sponge cake with a sweet-and-sour orange filling and coating it with chocolate, these once featured as the main focus in a legal case to determine whether they were actually biscuits (cookies) or, indeed as the name would suggest, cakes. Spoiler: they’re cakes . Since Jaffa Cakes are hard to find in Japan, these are a must-grab item if you visit the shop, and being sweet they make a perfect accompaniment to a cup of tea. Next up were the Somerset Cheddar and Shallot flavor Savoursmiths crisps . A high-end crisp brand from the UK comes at a price of 220 yen for a bag, which is definitely on the higher side when comparing other potato chips in a Japanese supermarket. The crunchy texture was exquisite, and we ended up finishing them before we had even realized it. Sometimes a trip to Tokyo is not easy, so there’s also the option of ordering from the shop online, where shipping is free on orders over 12,000 yen. The British Shop offers everything from classic snacks to slightly niche ingredients, with items such as bacon, bread, seasonings, and Yorkshire Tea Gold all available to purchase. If you’re not as unlucky as us when visiting the store, you’ll also get to try the quintessential British summertime treat of a 99 Flake all the way on the other side of the globe. title: Japanese government hires leading comedy agency to explain national defense spending
summary: The number one rule of comedy is unwavering loyalty to the government. I suppose in terms of things on a global scale, the Japanese government isn’t doing all that bad. It’s just that with all the talk of how Prime Minister Takaichi works constantly and rarely sleeps, I was sort of expecting something more in […]
details: The number one rule of comedy is unwavering loyalty to the government . I suppose in terms of things on a global scale, the Japanese government isn’t doing all that bad. It’s just that with all the talk of how Prime Minister Takaichi works constantly and rarely sleeps, I was sort of expecting something more in the way of results. Don’t get me wrong, since coming into power, her cabinet pissed off China right quick, jacked up visa fees , and made it so people can’t poop on the flag . These are all indeed things that were done, and yet, all those efforts don’t seem to have changed the fact that the cost of living in Japan keeps going up and that entire cities are on the verge of being taken over by bears and monkeys . One other thing the Takaichi cabinet has been hard at work at is amending the constitution of Japan to give the military more freedom to take action in overseas conflicts that may not directly threaten the safety of this country. Opponents of this idea say that it goes against the principles of Japan’s previously pacifist constitution, but maybe this is just a very complex situation in an increasingly destabilized world, which may have aspects not everyone is aware of. If only there was a sassy comedy duo that could explain it all in terms an average Joe can understand! And just like that, our prayers are answered. The Government Public Relations Office has teamed up with Japan’s leading comedy talent agency Yoshimoto Kogyo to produce a campaign that explains why some of the seemingly uninspiring things the government’s been doing are actually very good. Yoshimoto specializes in the style of comedy known as manzai . This is a bit of a throwback to the vaudeville era of Western comedy, often involving duos wherein one is the straight man ( tsukkomi ) and the other the funny man ( boke ). This particular series seems to employ a Burns and Allen style combo featuring the husband Kunio and wife Tamiyo, as they trade quips over national policy. ▼ A video trailer for the campaign The art of manzai is largely associated with the culture of Osaka, and is often best delivered in an Osaka dialect and accent, which I prefer to liken to a Staten Island accent, more or less based on vibes alone. There are currently seven pages where Kunio and Tamiyo crack wise about national policy in this manner of speaking, so let’s take a look at their talk about national defense. Tamiyo: “Did you know that Japan’s support ships help sustain our daily lives? They support the world, and Japan is supported as well.” Kunio: “Actually, more than 80 percent of the ships they protect belong to other countries! Japan helps to safeguard its allies, so the world protects Japan in return. We work together and look out for one another, ya know?” … Oh, that’s it? Hahahaha! Granted, it’s hard to make cooperative maritime defense funny, or at least, it’s hard when your job is being a government mouthpiece. Let’s see how they handle some softball topics like the space program instead. Tamiyo: “You ever take it for granted that we can go places we’ve never been before and don’t get lost?” Kunio: “Actually, we’re being guided from space. Japan’s Michibiki satellite system provides us with directions around the clock.” … Sorry, I was thinking about something else there. That one was quite a whiff too, wasn’t it? Alright, let’s take a look at their hot take on AI. This should be a slam dunk since the characters appear to have been hastily generated by AI themselves. Tamiyo: “You think since AI can help with things like planning meals or finding information, it can also be useful for national security?” Kunio: “Actually, efforts are underway to leverage AI so that it can help safeguard the nation.” … Jeez, they’re hardly even using an Osaka dialect in these. Getting a comedy routine down solid is hard work and takes time. We can at least see the seeds of the mansplaining premise beginning to sprout. It all makes me wonder if maybe I’m being too hard on the comedic stylings of Tamiyo and Kunio. Let’s see what online comments say about them. “Are they trying to brainwash us with propaganda now?” “The all-knowing man teaching his dimwitted wife. This really encapsulates why Japan ranks 114th out of 145 countries in the Global Gender Gap Index.” “This is the lowest form of propaganda. I’m done supporting Yoshimoto and won’t buy anything their performers do commercials for.” “They clearly think the public is stupid. They’re looking down on all of us.” “They must think we’re insanely gullible.” “It seems that the country is the role of the ‘husband,’ and the people are the ‘wife,’ which is also just creepy.” “There is no way this will foster understanding. Stop it immediately.” “Don’t waste our tax money on this garbage. If the Prime Minister would just show up in the Diet to provide proper answers or hold actual press conferences, this wouldn’t be necessary!” “This is very dystopian.” I scrolled far and wide and could not find anyone with an even remotely positive thing to say about this campaign. It does not bode well for the government, whose recent lifting of a ban on exporting lethal weapons is currently opposed by about 57 percent of the population, according to a poll by Japan’s Kyodo news organization . Kyodo also cites sources inside the government as saying that explanations of policy that avoid words like “lethal” would be more effective in swaying public opinion. That does sound a tad Orwellian, but we shouldn’t knock it till we try it, so let’s see what Tamiyo and Kunio have to say about the nation’s defense policy. Tamiyo: “You ever think we take uneventful days for granted?” Kunio: “Actually, the fact that nothing newsworthy happened today just goes to show ya. A day where ‘nothing happens’ ain’t no coincidence. It’s the result of tireless work to keep us safe.” Ha! Those two kill me. title: Starbucks Japan unveils new winter drinkware collection with limited-edition Stanley cups
summary: New collection brings warmth and style to tumblers and mugs this winter. When the seasons change in Japan, so too do the limited-edition goods at Starbucks, and this season we’ll be getting a new limited-edition collection just for winter. With icy hues of white and mint green, these items are said to blend easily into […]
details: New collection brings warmth and style to tumblers and mugs this winter. When the seasons change in Japan, so too do the limited-edition goods at Starbucks , and this season we’ll be getting a new limited-edition collection just for winter . With icy hues of white and mint green , these items are said to blend easily into any scenario to “softly illuminate your winter days”, and there are six specially designed products to choose from. ▼ Pale White Stanley Stainless Steel Bottle , 473 millilitres (16 ounces) – 6,350 yen (US$40.11) This leak-proof stainless steel bottle has a sleek and simple design, with a handle built into the lid for easy carrying. The body has a pale white colour that shimmers delicately in the light, adding an air of sophistication to your everyday drinking experience. This is one of the four items in the series that’s also eligible for Starbucks’ online store name engraving service, which lets you add your name and/or a pictogram to the back, bringing the total to 7,450 yen. ▼ Mint Green Stainless Steel To Go Tumbler – 473 millilitres (4,600 yen) The body of this stainless steel tumbler has a soothing mint green hue, while the shape is inspired by Starbucks’ paper cups, making it suitable for a wide range of scenarios, from everyday use to office settings. This product is also eligible for the online store’s personalisation service, which raises the price to 5,700 yen. ▼ Mint Green Logo Cold Cup Tumbler – 710 millilitres (3,050 yen) This tumbler features an eye-catching, diamond-cut design that gives off a different look depending on how the light hits it. The straw, which allows you to easily enjoy cold drinks, also has a textured surface that catches the light, adding a touch of elegance to your drink time. ▼ White Stainless Steel Cold Cup Tumbler – 591 millilitres (5,350 yen) This user-friendly tumbler features an easy-to-grip handle and a removable straw, for use with cold beverages only. With the personalisation service, the total price of the tumbler comes to 6,450 yen. ▼ Mint Green Stainless Steel Mug – 355 millilitres (3,800 yen) The mint green hues on this stainless steel mug add a sense of calmness to the simple design while the debossed Siren logo creates a subtle accent. The lid features a drinking spout and a slide-open mechanism for ease of use, and if you opt for the personalisation service the total comes to 4,900 yen. ▼ Mint Green Heat-resistant Glass Mug – 296 millilitres (3,500 yen) This glass mug features a unique base filled with glittery confetti that swirls about as you enjoy your drink. The transparent design allows you to enjoy the color of your drink alongside the elegant, sparkly confetti. The new collection is a beautiful way to add a sense of warmth and luxury to wintry drinks, and they can be purchased at Starbucks stores and online while stocks last. title: Giant Code Geass C.C. plush stands over three feet tall and costs $420
summary: C.C. from Code Geass is getting a plushie that turns the green-haired anime girl into a giant three-foot-tall collectible.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 Entertainment Giant Code Geass C.C. plush stands over three feet tall and costs $420 by James Busby Published: Nov 05, 2026, 11:03 Save for later Save for later TAITO GEAR&GOODS Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News C.C. from the popular anime Code Geass is getting a plushie that turns the green-haired girl into a giant three-foot-tall collectible. It’s been a big year for monolithic anime merch, with everything from a life-size Marin Kitagawa figure with an $8,000 price tag to giant Snorlax body pillows . However, fans of the popular mecha anime Code Geass will soon be able to celebrate the show’s 20th anniversary in style with a plushie so big that it needs its own dedicated spot on your sofa. Article continues after ad The massive merch in question is a three-foot-tall C.C. plushie that comes with the character’s signature vibrant green hair, white straitjacket, and a $420 price tag. Code Geass C.C. gets massive plushie According to the official store page , the plush recreates the white restraint outfit C.C. wears in her first appearance, including its black belts, fastenings, and long, flared sleeves. The C.C. plushie also comes with a hidden feature under the fringe, as her red Geass symbol has been embroidered on her forehead. Article continues after ad Article continues after ad As for just how much space she’ll take up, C.C. measures approximately 39.4 inches tall, 27.6 inches wide, and 29.5 inches deep. The polyester plush also weighs around 19.4 pounds, making this a particularly hefty addition to any Code Geass collection. TAITO GEAR&GOODS The made-to-order doll will be available to pre-order for residents in Japan from November 6, 2026 until December 21, with shipping scheduled for May 2027. It also comes with a pretty big price tag as well, as the store page lists C.C. for ¥66,000 (around $420). title: Dragon Ball Daima censored in France to erase Mr Popo, but fans can still hear him
summary: Dragon Ball Daima has completely removed Mr. Popo in France, with the character being edited out of scenes despite his voice remaining.
details: Trending Modern Warfare 4 Twitch EA FC 27 Wardogs GTA 6 TV & Movies Anime Dragon Ball Daima censored in France to erase Mr Popo, but fans can still hear him by Michael Gwilliam Published: Nov 05, 2026, 20:40 Save for later Save for later Crunchyroll Add as a preferred source on Google Follow on Google News Dragon Ball Daima has completely removed Mr. Popo from the screen in France, with the character being edited out of scenes despite his voice remaining in the anime. The latest installment in Akira Toriyama’s iconic franchise originally debuted in October 2024 , following Goku and his allies as they’re transformed into children and forced to venture into the Demon Realm. On November 4, 2026, Daima made its French television debut on Gulli, but viewers quickly noticed that one familiar character was nowhere to be seen. Article continues after ad As reported by Journal du Geek , Mr. Popo, the longtime attendant of Kami and later Dende, had been completely erased from the screen. Rather than simply cutting his dialogue, scenes featuring the character were removed, cropped, or edited to ensure he never appeared on camera. Strangely enough, however, his voice can still be heard in certain scenes, meaning the character technically still exists in the French version. Article continues after ad Mr Popo a été supprimé de Dragon Ball Daima en France ! Il parle, mais n'apparait pas à l'image !! LA HONTE 😑 @ToeiAnimationEU … Non mais sérieux…. pic.twitter.com/h1z5nxseaL — Tony Graci (@Tony_Mr_P) November 4, 2026 “Mr. Popo has been removed from Dragon Ball Daima in France! He speaks, but doesn’t appear on screen!” one furious fan wrote on X. Article continues after ad Another report indicated that Episode 2 received similar treatment, with scenes heavily re-edited and zoomed in to hide Mr. Popo. Why was Mr Popo censored in Dragon Ball Daima? The character’s design has been controversial for decades, with critics arguing that his dark skin, exaggerated red lips, and other features resemble racist caricatures. EN FRANCE, LE PERSONNAGE DE MR POPO DANS L’ANIME DRAGON BALL : DAIMA A ÉTÉ CENSURÉ ! ❌ La voix du personnage est présente dans les épisodes, mais il n’apparaît pas à l’écran. pic.twitter.com/bHBkeZXHex — INKU (@Inku_fr) November 4, 2026 However, defenders of the design argue that Mr. Popo was never intended to represent a black person. Fans have pointed to similarities with Mahakala , a dark-skinned guardian deity in Buddhist and Hindu traditions, suggesting his appearance draws from religious imagery rather than racist stereotypes. Related Dragon Ball Daima release date, trailer, & everything else you should know Dragon Ball Daima episode one anime details leak ahead of 2024 release Dragon Ball Daima divides fans with new character designs Article continues after ad This isn’t even the first time Dragon Ball has censored him. In the American CW broadcast of Dragon Ball Z Kai in 2010, Mr. Popo was famously recolored blue. France also isn’t the first country to remove him from Daima. Germany’s broadcast received similar edits when the anime premiered on Toggo Plus in August 2026. Article continues after ad It’s currently unclear whether the French censorship was ordered by Gulli or Toei Animation Europe, and neither has publicly confirmed the reason behind the changes. Article continues after ad The controversy is particularly notable given Toriyama’s involvement in Daima’s story and character designs , with the anime even offering new clues about Mr. Popo’s mysterious origins. For fans wanting to see the original version, all 20 episodes of Dragon Ball Daima are available uncensored with subtitles on streaming services including Crunchyroll and Netflix in France. title: Pachinko parlor operator arrested for not obscuring the act of gambling well enough
summary: If you’re going to do wrong, do wrong right. For many years, pachinko parlors have stood tall and proud in just about every community across the country as bastions of the human desire to make quick money without having to work for it. Every day, thousands and thousands of people flock to the large and […]
details: If you’re going to do wrong, do wrong right . For many years, pachinko parlors have stood tall and proud in just about every community across the country as bastions of the human desire to make quick money without having to work for it. Every day, thousands and thousands of people flock to the large and comfortably equipped complexes, seemingly never realizing that the main reason these places are so large and comfortably equipped is that they’re the ones ending up with the money. It should be noted that pachinko is technically not gambling, however. Japan has frowned on the vice of gambling for most of its history, with the exception of government-run operations of horse racing, boat racing, bicycle racing, and the lottery, as well as a recently enacted law allowing strictly managed casinos in integrated resorts. ▼ You get four forms of gambling and that’s it! OK, fine! Five, but that’s really it! Even when pachinko players win, they get no money awarded by the parlor . Depending on the performance of the player, they are awarded metal balls by the machine. They’re kind of like the tickets you’d get from a skee-ball machine, and in the same way, you can trade in the balls at a counter in the parlor for wonderful “special prizes” ( tokushu keihin ) . These prizes can be ordinary arbitrary items like pens or lighter flint, but many places nowadays award cards with tiny pieces of gold in them to help prevent counterfeiting. ▼ It takes a lot of balls to play this game. As luck would have it, right beside, or at least not too far from the pachinko parlor, there is always a store owned by people who seem to really love these special prizes. If you go here, you can sell them for ridiculously more than they’re actually worth and walk away with a nice chunk of change from a legitimate sale of your newfound special prizes . It’s a bit of a silly business model if you ask me, which must be why these places are often very modest-looking and have little to no signage. ▼ On your right is a pachinko parlor and on the left is a shop that buys prizes for a pachinko parlor. It may look like the same business, but that store is technically in a different building and owned by a different company, and what’s with all the questions anyway? What, are you a cop or something? Of course, since they offer such amazing prices for these prizes, they often end up with too many. But a lucky coincidence strikes again in the form of a wholesaler who is willing to buy those items from the shop, practically at cost, and sell them back to the pachinko parlors, once again, practically at cost . Since these are all legit sales, the government gets its piece of the action in the form of taxes, and everyone’s happy… except those players without wonderful special prizes, of whom there are many. This circle of life is called the “ santen hoshiki ” or “three-store system,” and it’s what separates dirty, yucky gambling from shiny, happy free-market capitalism. But should a pachinko parlor take it upon themselves to not follow the three-store system, trouble awaits, as it did recently in Miyagi Prefecture. On October 30th, it was reported that charges were filed against the manager and operating company of a pachinko parlor in the city of Ishinomaki. According to the charges, on 20 January, the parlor purchased four special prizes from a customer for a total of 3,500 yen (US$22), thus bypassing the three-store system and awarding cash prizes for games of chance. This parlor had since closed down, but the 71-year-old manager confessed to the act. This is the first such case to occur in Miyazaki since 2007. Readers of the news expressed understandable confusion in comments with regard to what the heck is actually going on with pachinko in Japan in the first place. “Seriously, why is the three-store system only permitted for pachinko parlors? Has that ever actually been explained?” “Why go through with all this superficial nonsense? Just ban pachinko for crying out loud.” “This is kind of absurd, isn’t it?” “In Asakusa [in Tokyo] there’s an exchange booth for a pachinko parlor right next to a police box.” “There’s probably some other crime involved they want to look into.” “Funny how pachinko parlor staff never seem to notice the mysterious little shacks sitting right on their own premises.” “The three-shop system is inherently illegal, isn’t it?” “I’ll just go and set up my own three-shop system then.” While it sounds like a great idea to set up your own casino and only give away prizes that can be cycled through the three-store system, that will likely land you in prison. As mentioned in the comments, this system is only applicable to pachinko and slot machines. All other games are regulated differently . Casino games are the most highly regulated, and if the house gives out so much as a mustache comb, they’ll get shut down faster than you can say, “A mustache comb? What the f…” Arcades, or “game centers” as they’re called in Japan, also have regulations on awarding prizes of any kind. One exception are UFO catchers, and this is mainly because in these games, the entire point is to grab the item. However, they are strictly regulated as well, and the prizes they offer cannot exceed a wholesale price of 1,000 yen per item. ▼ That’s a good fact to know when considering a lucky bag claw game . Another interesting example of pseudo-gambling in Japan are those high-end gacha machines where you pay 1,000 yen for a chance to get a Gucci bag or PS5 . The reason these aren’t gambling is because they aren’t even classified as games. They’re technically vending machines from which straight purchases are made, and they will be treated as such as long as the customer never “loses” in the sense of getting an empty capsule or booby prize. title: Pokémon doughnuts pop up at Mister Donut, with a new gathering that’s bigger than ever
summary: The “Everyone Gather Together! Winter Pokémon Campaign” goes all out for the 30th anniversary celebrations. It’s become something of an annual tradition for Mister Donut to release a new Pokémon collection at the end of the year, with a different pocket monster taking centre stage as the star of the show. This year, however, for […]
details: The “Everyone Gather Together! Winter Pokémon Campaign” goes all out for the 30th anniversary celebrations. It’s become something of an annual tradition for Mister Donut to release a new Pokémon collection at the end of the year, with a different pocket monster taking centre stage as the star of the show. This year, however, for Pokémon’s 30th anniversary , the chain is going all out with the celebrations, putting not just one Pokémon in the spotlight, but a whole gathering from past campaigns. ▼ The promo image reads “Atsumare! Minna!” (“Gather! Everyone!”) Image: Press release With this being the ninth Pokémon x Mister Donut collaboration collection, there are a lot of characters returning for the celebrations, and Mister Donut says every Pokémon that has appeared in previous collaborations will be coming together for this year’s collection. Leading the charge on the doughnut front is Alolan Diglett , who differs from the Diglett that appeared previously with a different coating and a gummy nose instead of a chocolate one. ▼ Oh, and a chocolate rendering of its head tuft, seeing as it’s Alolan. The theme for this year’s collaboration is “ Alolan Diglett Brings Everyone Together! ” and while the doughnuts are limited to Alolan Diglett and fan favourite Pikachu , the Pokémon gathering takes place on the limited-edition merchandise that can be bought as a set with the doughnuts. There’s also a cream-filled choux doughnut called “ Pokémon Friends Gather! Angel & Custard “, which comes in one of four randomly selected sleeves featuring the Pokémon characters. The “Goods Set” (2,200 yen for takeout, 2,217 yen for dine-in) gets you two Pokémon doughnuts of your choice, one doughnut from a choice of two “Pon de Wreath” varieties, a choice of one of two blankets, and an original paper bag. The “Kids Goods Set” gets you one Pokémon doughnut, one doughnut from the choice of two “Pon de Wreath” varieties, a limited-edition Pokémon glass and an original paper bag. ▼ We stopped by to get our hands on the “Goods Set”, which came in this gorgeous bag. When we returned home, we laid out our haul, and couldn’t help but admire the cute characters that sat in front of use, including on the doughnut box. Taking a closer look at the blanket, there are two to choose from, blue and orange, and we went for the orange one, which features plenty of Grass-type Pokémon and other warm-coloured characters. Each blanket has a different selection of Pokémon, so you can either choose the one that has your favourite characters, or purchase two sets to catch ’em all. The blankets look much the same as they do every year, but this time they seem to have been made slightly bigger. They’ve increased in height, making them closer to square than the horizontally elongated rectangles of previous years, giving you more coverage for use as a lap blanket, which is a welcome improvement. It is rather thin, though, and amounts to around 1,200 yen of the price of the set so it’s not entirely a bargain, but it is an exclusive you won’t find anywhere else so it’s still a sought-after item for fans. ▼ Last year’s blanket on top, compared to this year’s slightly larger version below. As for the doughnuts, they looked as cute as ever, and Alolan Diglett was particularly delicious, thanks to its chocolate-coated doughnut base and whipped-cream-filled centre. This year, Pikachu appears in its fluffy form for the second year running, and is still filled with the same whipped cream, with custard-flavoured flakes sprinkled across its surface. ▼ Like last year, Pikachu has rosy pink cheeks, even though they really ought to be red, if we’re going to be true to the character. Both doughnuts were as cute as they were delicious, but the party doesn’t end there, as Mister Donut says it will be bringing out a Slowpoke doughnut to join the collection from 25 November. ▼ Online reservations for the new doughnut begin on 18 November. Image: Press release The current Pokémon collection went on sale across Japan from 4 November, but only in limited stocks so you’ll want to head out early to find them or reserve them through Mister Donut’s online ordering service to ensure you don’t miss out. title: Discount retailers known for massive bargains releases massive Japanese egg sandwich
summary: Don Quijote doubles up its “Peculiar Preference” sandwich. Japanese egg sandwiches have recently become an unexpected hit among the international foodie community, but within Japan, they’ve been a staple for generations. You really don’t have to go very far to find one, as just about every convenience store or supermarket stocks them. But if you […]
details: Don Quijote doubles up its “Peculiar Preference” sandwich . Japanese egg sandwiches have recently become an unexpected hit among the international foodie community, but within Japan, they’ve been a staple for generations. You really don’t have to go very far to find one, as just about every convenience store or supermarket stocks them. But if you really love Japan’s egg sandwiches, it’s worth going to the little extra trouble of making a trip to discount retailer Don Quixote to get one, because not only are they massive, right now they’re even bigger than they usually are. Among tourists, Don Quijote is most famous for their selection of quirky souvenirs and affordable cosmetics, but they also sell clothing, toiletries, housewares, and, at some locations, even food items, including ready to eat bento boxed lunches and sandwiches. With the chain being popular with a broad range of shoppers, you’d expect them to want to offer foodstuffs that anyone would like. However, for their Henai Meshi , or “Peculiar Preference Food,” line, Don Quijote isn’t worried about fully satisfying everybody. In fact, the goal of Henai Meshi is to create meals “that most people would give 75 points out of 100, but that some people will give 120,” like the Bento with Fried Chicken Skin Only that they offered a while back. The Henai Meshi egg sandwich isn’t so unusual in terms of it ingredients, but their quantity could be considered egregious by some, as each sandwich is made with two and a half soft-boiled eggs. Right now, though, Don Quijote is running a special promotion in which it’s increasing the size of selected Henai Meshi items, and one of those is the egg sandwich, which has doubled in size and now contains five eggs! The Five Melty Soft-boiled Egg Sandwich is priced at 430 yen (US$2.70), and if you’re thinking it’s got to be hefty to hold, you’re exactly right. We were curious as to just how heavy it was, so once we got back to the SoraNews24 taste-testing center, before digging in we placed it on a scale… …which gave us a weight of 418 grams (roughly 14.75 ounces) . Granted, a small fraction of that is the plastic packaging, but still, this is close to a pound of eggs and bread . There’s so much egg that the strips of bread between them start to look like garnish, or maybe just something to keep your fingers clean as you eat a whole tray of eggs. Taste-testing was handled by our Japanese-language reporter P.K. Sanjun, who informs us that, in his estimation, the Five Melty Soft-boiled Egg Sandwich completely misses the mark for the Henai Meshi series. However, that’s not a complaint, because he clarifies that instead of being something that most people would give 75 point to and some would give 120, this sandwich is so delicious that he thinks most people would give it 95 out of a 100 . Of course, while we’re talking about numerical measurements, your dietician probably wouldn’t be too thrilled about what eating five eggs at once would do to your cholesterol levels. However, with Don Quiojote’s double-sized egg sandwich only being available from November 1 to 10 , there’s not time really enough time to do all that much dietary damage, making this a decadent special-occasion indulgence P.K. is very happy to have treated himself to. title: Tokyo to build new crematoriums to meet surging demand
summary: Death is a growth industry that no one’s happy about. There has been a lot of talk about the aging population in Japan and how it’s affecting society and the economy. But a more immediate concern is how to handle the influx of people currently dying across the country. According to estimates, the number of […]
details: Death is a growth industry that no one’s happy about . There has been a lot of talk about the aging population in Japan and how it’s affecting society and the economy. But a more immediate concern is how to handle the influx of people currently dying across the country. According to estimates, the number of deaths per year is expected to swell to a peak of 1.65 million in 2040, but with the current number over 1.5 million, Japan looks poised to overshoot that estimate considerably . Large cities in particular are starting to feel the strain, since the common method of internment in Japan is cremation. Luckily, this means cemetery space can be kept rather small, but the facilities to perform cremations are limited. There have been reports of crematoriums in Chiba Prefecture issuing wait times of as many as 10 days, and supply and demand has also seen the costs of such services rise as well. In normal businesses, this would attract other competitors who would eventually bring down prices, but that is especially difficult for crematoriums as they are very costly to set up and zoning laws make it very hard to even find a place to put a facility for burning human remains. ▼ Urayasu Crematorium is located right beside Tokyo Disneyland, you can see just a bit of it if you look to your left along with the Tokyo Skytree in the distance. Nowhere is this situation more severe then the dense metropolis of Tokyo, whose government recently decided to take matters into their own hands and are drafting a proposal to build a series of small-scale publicly run crematoriums throughout the 23 wards . They will focus on adding locations where they are needed most, and if necessary, relax zoning laws to allow them to fit. That’s not to say the private sector is sitting around doing nothing. In recent years, Japan has seen the emergence of what is colloquially called “itai hotels” (literally “corpse hotels”) . These are facilities that refrigerate the body so it is preserved until cremation can be made available, while also allowing loved ones to visit in a respectful, home-like environment. True to the name, they even offer rates comparable to a hotel’s, ranging from 10,000 to 200,000 per day depending on size and quality. ▼ News report showing the inside of an itai hotel The real difficulty in these projects is that, despite how serious the problem is now, it’s destined to be a temporary one because of Japan’s shrinking population , making it harder to make a case for large-scale infrastructure investment. At least if governments take the initiative in building new crematoriums, they can be shut down more easily when no longer needed, and itai hotels are more or less standard commercial facilities that can be easily repurposed. It’s an awkward situation that Japan is still trying to feel its way around, but it’s something many other countries are going to have to face in the coming years. Hopefully, others can learn from what goes right and what goes wrong here. title: Continuing cyberattacks hit Japanese arcade hard [Photos]
summary: Preserving arcade culture is hard enough without hacker jerks making it even tougher. A photo of an empty interior and unused game machines accompanied by the message “This is the harsh reality for arcades right now” might be the kind of thing that would make gamers sad, but not necessarily surprised. Though the video game […]
details: Preserving arcade culture is hard enough without hacker jerks making it even tougher . A photo of an empty interior and unused game machines accompanied by the message “This is the harsh reality for arcades right now” might be the kind of thing that would make gamers sad, but not necessarily surprised. Though the video game business as a whole is bigger than ever, the ways that people play them has changed significantly since the arcade glory days of the ‘80s and ‘90s, and the industry trend in Japan has become one of arcades steadily reducing the amount of floorspace they devote to video games while installing more and more UFO catcher/crane/claw prize machines. But a recent tweet from the Machida branch of arcade chain Taito Station in Tokyo doesn’t show just row after row of unoccupied games, but ones with dark screens too . ゲームセンターの過酷な現状… お客様の皆様には大変御迷惑お掛けしています。 pic.twitter.com/gF1YjwSEZ9 — タイステ町田 (@Taito_Machida) November 5, 2026 The reason for all that dark emptiness isn’t because the arcade’s entire customer base decided they’d rather be somewhere else playing Fortnite on their phones. No, it’s because, as with so many other things these days, of the huge increase in hacks, cyberattacks, and other online maliciousness and jackassery over the past few weeks. One of the ways the surviving arcade video game franchises have survived is by embracing online/network play, especially if it’s coupled to some sort of deluxe control or display hardware that would be impractically large or expensive for many people’s homes, such as a full steering wheel and pedals, expansive dance step sensors, card readers, or gigantic touchscreen arrays. Combine that feeling of immersion with the ability to race, fight, or otherwise compete with other players, either in real-time or through leaderboards, and you can cultivate a customer community by connecting modestly sized, geographically separated pockets of fans. Unfortunately, that means that if a game network’s security is compromised and it has to be shut down, either in response to a hack or as a preventive measure, the game has to be shut down too . Network play is so integrated into many Japanese arcade games that the first thing they do upon booting up is try to connect to their network, and some can’t progress to a playable state until they can successfully do so, resulting in situations like the one shown in the Taito Station Machida tweet, in which the arcade says “We deeply apologize for the great inconvenience to our customers.” 一角は営業中かも危ぶまれるような写真ですがちゃんと稼働しているゲームも勿論有りますので是非ともご利用下さいね！ #タイステ #町田 pic.twitter.com/bcDo1HmieB — タイステ町田 (@Taito_Machida) November 5, 2026 Thankfully, not every game in the arcade has had to go offline, and classic titles that don’t require a network connection are unaffected , so, as shown in the above follow-up tweet, Taito Station Matsuda still has games that can be played, and they invite gamers to come in for them. Other arcades are likely dealing with similar problems, so if you’re a gamer with a few spare 100-yen coins in your wallet, they’d probably appreciate a visit, even if your regular favorites aren’t currently playable.
